bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第271卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 271
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 271

sentences.zh: 【後梁紀六】起屠維單閼十月，盡玄黓敦牂，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: 【Later Liang Records 6】 From the tenth month of the year jiyou in the sexagenary cycle to the year xuanchou, a total of three years and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: 【Later Liang Records 6】 Spanning from the tenth month of jiyou through xuanchou in the sexagenary cycle—three years and a fraction in all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，出濛為楚州團練使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Meng was dismissed as regent and appointed military commissioner of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Yang Meng was removed from his regency and made regimental commissioner of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王如魏州，發徒數萬，廣德勝北城，日與梁人爭，大小百餘戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin went to Weizhou, mobilized tens of thousands of laborers, and expanded the northern wall of Desheng; day by day he contended with the Liang forces, fighting more than a hundred engagements large and small, with victory alternating between them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxu, Prince of Jin, traveled to Weizhou and drafted tens of thousands of workers to enlarge Desheng's north wall. Day after day he skirmished with the Liang army—over a hundred clashes, large and small, with neither side holding a lasting edge.

sentences.zh: 左射軍使石敬瑭與梁人戰於河壖，梁人擊敬瑭，斷其馬甲，橫衝兵馬使劉知遠以所乘馬授之，自乘斷甲者徐行為殿；

translations.literal: The Left Shear Army commissioner Shi Jingtang fought the Liang at the river embankment; the Liang struck Jingtang and severed his horse's armor; the Vanguard Cavalry commissioner Liu Zhiyuan gave him his own mount and himself rode the horse with broken armor, advancing slowly as rearguard;
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Shi Jingtang of the Left Shear Army battled Liang troops on the river levee. They struck him hard enough to shear his horse's barding. Liu Zhiyuan, commissioner of the Vanguard Cavalry, handed over his own horse and rode the damaged mount at an unhurried pace to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 梁人疑有伏，不敢追，俱得免，敬瑭以是親愛之。

translations.literal: The Liang suspected an ambush and dared not pursue; both escaped, and Jingtang thereafter held him in affection.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang suspected a trap and held back. Both men escaped, and from that day Jingtang cherished Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭、知遠，其先皆沙陀人。

translations.literal: Jingtang and Zhiyuan were both of Shatuo descent by origin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang and Zhiyuan both traced their ancestry to the Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭，李嗣源之婿也。

translations.literal: Jingtang was the son-in-law of Li Siyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was married to a daughter of Li Siyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩圍張萬進於兗州經年，城中危窘，晉王方與梁人戰河上，力不能救。

translations.literal: Liu Xun besieged Zhang Wanjin in Yanzhou for a year; the city was in dire peril; the Prince of Jin was then fighting the Liang on the river and lacked strength to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun had kept Zhang Wanjin bottled up in Yanzhou for a year. Inside the walls supplies ran thin. The Prince of Jin was fully engaged against Liang forces along the Yellow River and could not spare troops for a rescue.

sentences.zh: 萬進遣親將劉處讓乞師於晉，晉王未之許，處讓於軍門截耳曰：「苟不得請，生不如死！」

translations.literal: Wanjin sent his trusted officer Liu Churang to beg troops from Jin; the Prince of Jin did not consent; Churang at the army gate cut off his ear and said: "If I cannot obtain the request, life is worse than death!
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin dispatched his confidant Liu Churang to plead for Jin reinforcements. The prince refused. At the camp gate Churang sliced off his own ear and cried, "If you will not help us, death is kinder than this life!

sentences.zh: 晉王義之，將為出兵，會鄩已屠兗州，族萬進，乃止。

translations.literal: 」The Prince of Jin admired his resolve and was about to send troops, but Xun had already slaughtered Yanzhou and exterminated Wanjin's clan, so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Moved by his devotion, the prince prepared to march—but Liu Xun had already overrun Yanzhou and wiped out Wanjin's household, so the expedition was called off.

sentences.zh: 以處讓為行台左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Churang was appointed Left Valiant Guard general of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Churang was made Left Valiant Guard general on the prince's field staff.

sentences.zh: 處讓，滄州人也。

translations.literal: Churang was a man of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Churang came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，吳武寧節度使張崇寇安州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wu's Wuning military commissioner Zhang Chong raided Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Chong, military commissioner of Wuning in Wu, attacked Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以劉鄩為泰寧節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Liu Xun was made Taining military commissioner and associate chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Liu Xun received the posts of Taining military commissioner and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，王瓚引兵至戚城，與李嗣源戰，不利。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Wang Zan led troops to Qicheng and fought Li Siyuan, with an unfavorable outcome.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Wang Zan marched to Qicheng and clashed with Li Siyuan, coming off the worse.

sentences.zh: 梁築壘貯糧於潘張，距楊村五十里，十二月，晉王自將騎兵自河南岸西上，邀其餉者，俘獲而還；

translations.literal: The Liang built fortifications and stored grain at Panzhang, fifty li from Yangcun; in the twelfth month the Prince of Jin personally led cavalry west along the south bank of the river, intercepted their supply parties, captured them, and returned;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang fortified Panzhang and stockpiled grain fifty li from Yangcun. In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin led cavalry up the south bank, waylaid Liang supply columns, took prisoners and booty, and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 梁人伏兵於要路，晉兵大敗。

translations.literal: The Liang laid ambush on the vital road, and the Jin army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liang troops ambushed the route and routed the Jin force.

sentences.zh: 晉王以數騎走，梁數百騎圍之，李紹榮識其旗，單騎奮擊救之，僅免。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin fled with a few horsemen; several hundred Liang horsemen surrounded him; Li Shaorong recognized his banner, charged alone to rescue him, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The prince broke away with only a handful of riders. Hundreds of Liang cavalry ringed him. Li Shaorong spotted his standard and charged in alone to break the ring; the prince escaped by a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，晉王復與王瓚戰於河南，瓚先勝，獲晉將石君立等；

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Prince of Jin again fought Wang Zan south of the river; Zan won at first and captured the Jin general Shi Junli and others;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the prince met Wang Zan again south of the Yellow River. Zan struck first and took the Jin commander Shi Junli among others;

sentences.zh: 既而大敗，乘小舟渡河，走保北城，失亡萬計。

translations.literal: then suffered a great defeat, crossed the river in a small boat, fled to hold the north city, and lost tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: then was smashed in turn. Zan crossed in a skiff, fell back to the north citadel, and left tens of thousands dead or missing.

sentences.zh: 帝聞石君立勇，欲將之，繫於獄而厚餉之，使人誘之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Shi Junli was brave and wished to employ him; he imprisoned him but richly supplied him and sent men to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor heard of Junli's valor and wanted him in service. He was jailed but lavished with gifts while envoys tried to win him over.

sentences.zh: 君立曰：「我晉之敗將，而為用於梁，雖竭誠效死，誰則信之！

translations.literal: Junli said: "I am a defeated general of Jin, yet employed by Liang; though I exhaust loyalty unto death, who would believe it!
translations.idiomatic: Junli replied, "I am a beaten Jin officer. If I now serve Liang, even dying in earnest—who would trust me!

sentences.zh: 人各有君，何忍反為仇讎用哉！」

translations.literal: Each man has his lord; how could I bear to be used by the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Every man has his sovereign. How could I let my enemy wield me!"

sentences.zh: 帝猶惜之，盡殺所獲晉將，獨置君立。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor still prized him, executed all captured Jin generals, and alone spared Junli.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor still regretted losing him. Every other captured Jin commander was put to death; only Junli was spared.

sentences.zh: 晉王乘勝遂拔濮陽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin pressed the victory and then took Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the momentum, the Prince of Jin seized Puyang.

sentences.zh: 帝召王瓚還，以天平節度使戴思遠代為北面招討使，屯河上以拒晉人。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled Wang Zan and replaced him as northern campaign commissioner with the Tianping military commissioner Dai Siyuan, who encamped on the river to resist the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Wang Zan and named Dai Siyuan of Tianping northern campaign commissioner in his stead, stationing him along the river to block the Jin.

sentences.zh: 己酉，蜀雄武節度使兼中書令王宗朗有罪，削奪官爵，復其姓名曰全師朗，命武定節度使兼中書令桑弘志討之。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Shu Xiongwu military commissioner and chief councilor Wang Zonglang was guilty; his titles were stripped and his original name Quan Shilang restored; Wuding military commissioner and chief councilor Sang Hongzhi was ordered to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wang Zonglang—Xiongwu commissioner and chief councilor in Shu—was found guilty. His offices were revoked and his birth name Quan Shilang restored. Sang Hongzhi of Wuding was sent to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 吳禁民私畜兵器，盜賊益繁。

translations.literal: Wu forbade the people to keep weapons privately, and bandits grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wu banned private arms among the populace, and robbery only multiplied.

sentences.zh: 御史台主簿京兆盧樞上言：「今四方分爭，宜教民戰。

translations.literal: Censorate registrar Lu Shu of Jingzhao submitted: "Now the four quarters are divided in strife; the people ought to be taught warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shu, registrar of the Censorate from Jingzhao, memorialized: "The realm is split by war on every side. The people should be trained to fight.

sentences.zh: 且善人畏法禁而奸民弄乾戈，是欲偃武而反招盜也。

translations.literal: Moreover the good fear legal prohibitions while the wicked wield arms—this is wishing to lay down arms yet instead inviting robbers.
translations.idiomatic: The law-abiding fear the ban while rogues brandish weapons anyway—an attempt to pacify that only feeds the bandits.

sentences.zh: 宜團結民兵，使之習戰，自衛鄉里。」

translations.literal: Militia should be organized, trained in warfare, and made to defend their own districts.
translations.idiomatic: Organize militia, drill them, and let each community defend itself.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: 」The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊辰，蜀桑弘志克金州，執全師朗，獻於成都，蜀主釋之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on wuchen, Shu's Sang Hongzhi took Jinzhou, seized Quan Shilang, presented him at Chengdu, and the Shu ruler released him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuchen, Sang Hongzhi of Shu captured Jinzhou and Quan Shilang, brought him to Chengdu, and the Shu ruler set him free.

sentences.zh: 吳張崇攻安州，不克而還。

translations.literal: Wu: Zhang Chong attacked Anzhou, failed to take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Zhang Chong besieged Anzhou, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 崇在廬州，貪暴不法。

translations.literal: Chong was at Luzhou, greedy, violent, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ruled Luzhou with greed and brutality, heedless of law.

sentences.zh: 廬江民訟縣令受賕，徐知誥遣侍御史知雜事楊廷式往按之，欲以威崇，廷式曰：「雜端推事，其體至重，職業不可不行。」

translations.literal: Lujiang people sued the magistrate for taking bribes; Xu Zhigao sent investigating censor Yang Tingshi to examine the case, wishing to awe Chong; Tingshi said: "The miscellaneous censor's investigation is weighty in form; the duty cannot go unperformed.
translations.idiomatic: People of Lujiang accused their magistrate of bribery. Xu Zhigao sent Yang Tingshi, censor on miscellaneous matters, to investigate—hoping to intimidate Chong. Tingshi said, "A censor's inquiry carries grave weight. The duty must be carried out.

sentences.zh: 知誥曰：「何如？」

translations.literal: 」Zhigao said: "How then?
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhigao asked, "What do you propose?

sentences.zh: 廷式曰：「械系張崇，使吏如升州，簿責都統。」

translations.literal: 」Tingshi said: "Shackle Zhang Chong, send officers to Shengzhou, and audit the commander-in-chief's accounts.
translations.idiomatic: 」Tingshi answered, "Put Zhang Chong in irons, send clerks to Shengzhou, and audit the regional commander's books.

sentences.zh: 知誥曰：「所按者縣令耳，何至於是！」

translations.literal: 」Zhigao said: "The investigation targets only the magistrate—why go so far!
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhigao protested, "We are only looking into a county magistrate—why escalate like this!"

sentences.zh: 廷式曰：「縣令微官，張崇使之取民財轉獻都統耳，豈可捨大而詰小乎！」

translations.literal: 」Tingshi said: "The magistrate is a petty office; Chong had him squeeze the people and pass the wealth to the commander—how can we abandon the great and pursue the small!
translations.idiomatic: 」Tingshi replied, "A magistrate is a minor post. Chong used him to wring the people and funnel silver to the commander. Why chase the clerk and let the chief walk free!"

sentences.zh: 知誥謝之曰：「固知小事不足相煩。」

translations.literal: 」Zhigao apologized: "I knew from the start that a small matter was unworthy of troubling you.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhigao apologized. "I should have known a trifle was beneath your notice.

sentences.zh: 以是益重之。

translations.literal: 」Thereby he esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: 」From that day he held Tingshi in higher regard.

sentences.zh: 廷式，泉州人也。

translations.literal: Tingshi was a man of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshi came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王自得魏州，以李建及為魏博內外牙都將，將銀槍效節都。

translations.literal: Since the Prince of Jin took Weizhou, he made Li Jianji commander of Weibo's inner and outer guard, leading the Silver Spear Effectiveness Corps.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Weizhou, the prince appointed Li Jianji commander of Weibo's palace guard and head of the Silver Spear Effectiveness Corps.

sentences.zh: 建及為人忠壯，所得賞賜，悉分士卒，與同甘苦，故能得其死力，所向立功；

translations.literal: Jianji was loyal and stalwart; all rewards received he divided among the soldiers, sharing hardship and ease, and thus could obtain their utmost effort and win merit wherever he went;
translations.idiomatic: Jianji was loyal and fearless. Every reward he shared with his men, eating and marching as they did, and they repaid him with their lives on every campaign;

sentences.zh: 同列疾之。

translations.literal: his peers resented him.
translations.idiomatic: his peers grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 宦者韋令圖監建及軍，譖於晉王曰：「建及以私財驟施，此其志不小，不可使將牙兵。」

translations.literal: The eunuch Wei Lingtu supervised Jianji's army and slandered him to the Prince of Jin: "Jianji lavishes private wealth in sudden gifts—his ambition is no small matter; he must not be allowed to command the guard.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wei Lingtu, overseeing Jianji's command, whispered to the prince, "He showers the ranks with his own coin—ambition on that scale is dangerous. Do not let him keep the guard.

sentences.zh: 王疑之。

translations.literal: 」The prince grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince began to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 建及知之，自恃無它，行之自若。

translations.literal: Jianji knew of it, trusting he had no other fault, and acted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji heard of the suspicion but, confident he had done nothing wrong, carried on as usual.

sentences.zh: 三月，王罷建及軍職，以為代州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month the prince removed Jianji from military office and made him prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the prince stripped him of command and appointed him prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢楊洞潛請立學校，開貢舉，設銓選；

translations.literal: Han: Yang Dongqian requested establishing schools, opening the examination system, and instituting selection procedures;
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Yang Dongqian urged founding schools, reviving civil examinations, and setting up an appointment process;

sentences.zh: 漢主巖從之。

translations.literal: the Han ruler Yan complied.
translations.idiomatic: and the Han ruler Yan agreed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，以尚書右丞李琪為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yihai, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Qi was made Secretariat Vice Director and associate chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, Li Qi rose from vice director of the Secretariat to vice director of the Chancellery and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 琪，珽之弟也，性疏俊，挾趙巖、張漢傑之勢，頗通賄賂。

translations.literal: Qi was the younger brother of Ting; open and handsome in nature, he relied on the power of Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie and widely trafficked in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was younger brother to Ting—open-handed, handsome, and brazen. Backed by Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie, he traded freely in favors and bribes.

sentences.zh: 蕭頃與琪同為相，頃謹密而陰伺琪短。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiang served as chief councilor alongside Qi; Xiang was careful and secretive and secretly watched for Qi's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiang shared the premiership with Qi. Careful and close-mouthed, he watched for slips.

sentences.zh: 久之，有以攝官求仕者，琪輒改攝為守，頃奏之。

translations.literal: After a long while someone sought office as acting official; Qi promptly changed acting to regular appointment; Xiang memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: In time a man sought a post while serving only as acting officer. Qi upgraded acting status to full appointment. Xiang reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲流琪遠方，趙、張左右之，止罷為太子少保。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and wished to exile Qi to a distant place; Zhao and Zhang intervened on his behalf, and he was merely demoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor flew into a rage and meant to banish Qi. Zhao and Zhang pleaded for him, and the sentence was reduced to dismissal as Junior Mentor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使冀王友謙以兵襲取同州，逐忠武節度使程全暉，全暉奔大梁。

translations.literal: Hezhong military commissioner Prince of Ji Zhu Youqian seized Tongzhou by force, drove out Zhongwu military commissioner Cheng Quanhui, and Quanhui fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian, Prince of Ji and commissioner of Hezhong, stormed Tongzhou and expelled Cheng Quanhui, Zhongwu commissioner, who fled to the Liang capital at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 友謙以其子令德為忠武留後，表求節鉞，帝怒，不許。

translations.literal: Youqian made his son Lingde acting Zhongwu commissioner and memorialized for the seal and axe; the Emperor was angry and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Youqian installed his son Lingde as acting Zhongwu commissioner and petitioned for the full commission. The emperor refused in anger.

sentences.zh: 既而懼友謙怨望，己酉，以友謙兼忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Then fearing Youqian's resentment, on jiyou he was also made Zhongwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon fearing Youqian's bitterness, on jiyou the court added Zhongwu commissioner to his titles.

sentences.zh: 制下，友謙已求節鉞於晉王，晉王以墨制除令德忠武節度使。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, Youqian had already sought the seal and axe from the Prince of Jin, who by informal order made Lingde Zhongwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Youqian had already asked the Prince of Jin for the commission. The prince issued an informal appointment making Lingde Zhongwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳宣王重厚恭恪，徐溫父子專政，王未嘗有不平之意形於言色，溫以是安之。

translations.literal: Wu Prince of Xuan was grave, courteous, and respectful; Xu Wen and his son held power; the prince never showed discontent in word or countenance, and Wen was thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuan in Wu was grave and courteous. Xu Wen and his son ran the state, yet the prince never let resentment show in face or speech, and Wen took comfort in that.

sentences.zh: 及建國稱制，尤非所樂，多沉飲鮮食，遂成寢疾。

translations.literal: When the state was founded and he assumed imperial style, he liked it even less, drank heavily and ate rich foods, and thus fell into a wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu declared itself an empire he liked it even less. He drowned himself in wine and rich food until a wasting sickness took hold.

sentences.zh: 五月，溫自金陵入朝，議當為嗣者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wen entered court from Jinling to discuss who should be heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wen came from Jinling to court to settle the succession.

sentences.zh: 或希溫意言曰：「蜀先主謂武侯：『嗣子不才，君宜自取。』」

translations.literal: Someone hoping to please Wen said: "Shu's founding lord told the Martial Marquis: 'The heir lacks talent; you should take it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Someone eager to please Wen quoted the Shu founder's words to Zhuge Liang: "The heir lacks talent—you should take the throne yourself.

sentences.zh: 溫正色曰：「吾果有意取之，當在誅張顥之初，豈至今日邪！

translations.literal: 』" Wen said sternly: "If I truly meant to take it, I would have done so when Zhang Hao was executed at the beginning—how could it come to today!
translations.idiomatic: 』" Wen's face hardened. "If I had wanted the throne, I would have taken it when Zhang Hao was killed—not waited until now!

sentences.zh: 使楊氏無男，有女亦當立之。

translations.literal: Even if the Yang house had no sons, a daughter should still be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Yang line lacked sons, a daughter would still inherit.

sentences.zh: 敢妄言者斬！」

translations.literal: Whoever speaks rashly shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who speaks such nonsense loses his head!

sentences.zh: 乃以王命迎丹楊公溥監國，徙溥兄濛為舒州團練使。

translations.literal: 」Then by royal command Dan Yang Duke Pu was welcomed as regent, and Pu's elder brother Meng was moved to regimental commissioner of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 」By the prince's order, Yang Pu of Danyang was summoned as regent, and Pu's elder brother Meng was posted to Shuzhou as regimental commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己丑，宣王殂。

translations.literal: On jichou the Prince of Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Prince of Xuan died.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，溥即吳王位。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wushen, Pu assumed the kingship of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Pu took the throne of Wu.

sentences.zh: 尊母王氏曰太妃。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Wang was honored as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wang, was styled Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，蜀以司徒兼門下侍郎、同平章事周庠同平章事，充永平節度使。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Shu made Minister of Works and Chancellery Vice Director Zhou Xiang associate chief councilor and Yongping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Shu confirmed Zhou Xiang—already Minister of Works and Chancellery vice director—as associate chief councilor and named him Yongping military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝以泰寧節度使劉鄩為河東道招討使，帥感化節度使尹皓、靜勝節度使溫昭圖、莊宅使段凝攻同州。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Taining military commissioner Liu Xun Hezhong campaign commissioner, leading Ganhua military commissioner Yin Hao, Jingsheng military commissioner Wen Zhaotu, and estate commissioner Duan Ning to attack Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor appointed Liu Xun of Taining as Hezhong campaign commissioner, with Yin Hao of Ganhua, Wen Zhaotu of Jingsheng, and Duan Ning of the palace estates to besiege Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚申朔，蜀主作高祖原廟於萬里橋，帥后妃、百官用褻味作鼓吹祭之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, first day gengshen, the Shu ruler built the Founding Emperor's original temple at Wanli Bridge, leading consorts and officials to offer coarse foods with music in worship.
translations.idiomatic: On the intercalary month's gengshen new moon, the Shu ruler built a shrine to the founding emperor at Wanli Bridge and led consorts and officials in a raucous offering of humble foods.

sentences.zh: 華陽尉張士喬上疏諫，以為非禮，蜀主怒，欲誅之，太后以為不可，乃削官流黎州，士喬感憤，赴水死。

translations.literal: Huayang commandant Zhang Shiqiao memorialized in remonstrance, deeming it improper ritual; the Shu ruler was angry and wished to execute him; the empress dowager said it could not be done; his office was stripped and he was exiled to Lizhou; Shiqiao, indignant, drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiqiao, commandant of Huayang, protested that the rite was improper. The Shu ruler raged and wanted him killed until the empress dowager intervened. He was demoted and banished to Lizhou. Shiqiao, in despair, threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩等圍同州，朱友謙求救於晉。

translations.literal: Liu Xun and others besieged Tongzhou; Zhu Youqian begged rescue from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun's coalition tightened the siege of Tongzhou, and Zhu Youqian appealed to the Prince of Jin for aid.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，晉王遣李存審、李嗣昭、李建及、慈州刺史李存質將兵救之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Prince of Jin sent Li Cunshen, Li Sizhao, Li Jianji, and Cizhou prefect Li Cunzhi with troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the prince dispatched Li Cunshen, Li Sizhao, Li Jianji, and Li Cunzhi of Cizhou with an army to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，蜀主下詔北巡，以禮部尚書兼成都尹長安韓昭為文思殿大學士，位在翰林承旨上。

translations.literal: On yimao the Shu ruler decreed a northern tour, made Minister of Rites and Chengdu intendant Han Zhao of Chang'an Grand Academician of the Wensi Hall, ranking above the Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Shu ruler announced a northern progress and named Han Zhao of Chang'an—Minister of Rites and Chengdu intendant—Grand Academician of the Wensi Hall, senior even to the Hanlin chief.

sentences.zh: 昭無文學，以便佞得幸，出入宮禁，就蜀主乞通、渠、巴、集數州刺史賣之以營居第，蜀主許之。

translations.literal: Zhao lacked learning, gained favor through flattery, entered and left the palace precincts, begged the Shu ruler for the prefectures of Tong, Qu, Ba, and Ji to sell their offices and fund a mansion, and the Shu ruler granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had no scholarship but won favor by flattery, drifting freely through the inner palace. He asked the ruler to let him sell the prefectures of Tong, Qu, Ba, and Ji to fund a mansion—and the ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 識者知蜀之將亡。

translations.literal: The knowing perceived that Shu was about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Observers knew Shu was nearing its end.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰，蜀主發成都，被金甲，冠珠帽，執弓矢而行，旌旗兵甲，亙百餘里。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on wuchen, the Shu ruler departed Chengdu clad in golden armor, crowned with a jeweled cap, bearing bow and arrows as he marched; banners and armor stretched for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuchen, the Shu ruler left Chengdu in golden armor and a jeweled cap, bow in hand. Banners and steel filled the road for a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 雒令段融上言：「不宜遠離都邑，當委大臣征討。」

translations.literal: Luoyang magistrate Duan Rong submitted: "It is not fitting to stray far from the capital; great ministers should be entrusted with the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Rong, magistrate of Luoyang, urged, "The capital should not be left so lightly. Entrust the campaign to your ministers.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: 」He did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: 」He ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 九月，次安遠城。

translations.literal: Ninth month, he halted at Anyuan city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he encamped at Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 李存審等至河中，即日濟河。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen and others reached Hezhong and crossed the river the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen's column reached Hezhong and crossed the Yellow River that same day.

sentences.zh: 梁人素輕河中兵，每戰必窮追不置。

translations.literal: The Liang had always despised Hezhong troops and in every battle pursued relentlessly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang had long scorned Hezhong soldiers and pressed every pursuit to the limit.

sentences.zh: 存審選精甲二百，雜河中兵，直壓劉鄩壘，鄩出千騎逐之；

translations.literal: Cunshen selected two hundred elite armored men mixed with Hezhong troops and pressed straight on Liu Xun's camp; Xun sent out a thousand horsemen to pursue them;
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen picked two hundred armored elites, mingled them with Hezhong troops, and drove straight at Liu Xun's camp. Xun sent a thousand horsemen in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 知晉人已至，大驚，自是不敢輕出。

translations.literal: learning the Jin had arrived, he was greatly alarmed and thereafter dared not sally lightly.
translations.idiomatic: then learned the Jin army had come. He was shaken and no longer risked casual sorties.

sentences.zh: 晉人軍於朝邑。

translations.literal: The Jin encamped at Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin forces camped at Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 河中事梁久，將士皆持兩端。

translations.literal: Hezhong had long served Liang; officers and soldiers all hedged between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong had served Liang for years, and its officers wavered between allegiances.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大集，芻粟踴貴，友謙諸子說友謙且歸款於梁，以退其師，友謙曰：「昔晉王親赴吾急，秉燭夜戰。

translations.literal: Armies massed; fodder and grain soared in price; Youqian's sons urged him to submit to Liang to make the armies withdraw; Youqian said: "Long ago the Prince of Jin came in person to my distress and fought by candlelight through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Armies converged and fodder prices soared. Youqian's sons urged him to submit to Liang and send the invaders home. Youqian answered, "The Prince of Jin once came himself to my aid and fought through the night by candlelight.

sentences.zh: 今方與梁相拒，又命將星行，分我資糧，豈可負邪！」

translations.literal: Now while contending with Liang he again sends his star generals, sharing my stores—how could I betray him!
translations.idiomatic: Now, even as he battles Liang, he sends his best commanders and shares his stores with me—how could I turn on him!"

sentences.zh: 晉人分兵攻華州，壞其外城。

translations.literal: The Jin divided forces to attack Huazhou and destroyed its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Jin detachments struck Huazhou and breached its outer walls.

sentences.zh: 李存審等按兵累旬，乃進逼劉鄩營，鄩等悉眾出戰，大敗，收餘眾退保羅文寨。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen and others held their armies for many tens of days, then advanced on Liu Xun's camp; Xun and others led out all their forces, suffered a great defeat, gathered the remainder, and withdrew to hold Luowen stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen held his lines for weeks, then pressed Liu Xun's camp. Xun marched out with his full strength, was shattered, and fell back to Luowen stockade with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 又旬餘，存審謂李嗣昭曰：「獸窮則搏，不如開其走路，然後擊之。」

translations.literal: After another ten-odd days Cunshen said to Li Sizhao: "A beast cornered will fight—better to open its escape route, then strike it.
translations.idiomatic: Another fortnight on, Cunshen told Li Sizhao, "Cornered beasts fight hardest. Open a line of retreat, then hit them.

sentences.zh: 乃遣人牧馬於沙苑。

translations.literal: 」He then sent men to pasture horses at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: 」He sent men to graze horses openly at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 鄩等宵遁，追擊至渭水，又破之，殺獲甚眾，存審等移檄告諭關右，引兵略地至下邽，謁唐帝陵，哭之而還。

translations.literal: Xun and others fled by night; pursuit reached the Wei River and defeated them again, killing and capturing in great numbers; Cunshen and others issued proclamations to instruct the lands west of the pass, led troops to seize territory as far as Xiaji, visited the Tang imperial tombs, wept before them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's army slipped away at night. The pursuers caught them at the Wei River and broke them again with heavy slaughter. Cunshen proclaimed order west of the pass, marched as far as Xiaji, wept at the Tang imperial tombs, and turned home.

sentences.zh: 河中兵進攻崇州，靜勝節度使溫昭圖甚懼。

translations.literal: Hezhong troops advanced on Chongzhou; Jingsheng military commissioner Wen Zhaotu was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong forces pressed Chongzhou, and Wen Zhaotu, Jingsheng commissioner, was terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝使供奉官竇維說之曰：「公所有者華原、美原兩縣耳，雖名節度使，實一鎮將，比之雄籓，豈可同日語也，公有意欲之乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent palace attendant Dou Wei to persuade him: "What you hold is only the two counties of Huayuan and Meiyuan; though titled military commissioner, you are in truth a garrison commander—compared to great feudatories, how can they be spoken of in one breath; do you wish for such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor sent Dou Wei to sound him out: "You hold only Huayuan and Meiyuan. You bear the title of commissioner but rule like a garrison captain—nothing like the great frontier lords. Would you want something better?"

sentences.zh: 昭圖曰：「然。」

translations.literal: 」Zhaotu said: "Indeed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhaotu said, "I would."

sentences.zh: 維曰：「當為公圖之。」

translations.literal: 」Wei said: "I shall plot it for you.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wei replied, "Leave it to me."

sentences.zh: 即教昭圖表求移鎮，帝以汝州防禦使華溫琪權知靜勝留後。

translations.literal: 」He then had Zhaotu memorialize requesting transfer; the Emperor made Ruzhou defender Hua Wenqi acting Jingsheng regent.
translations.idiomatic: 」He coached Zhaotu to petition for a transfer. The emperor named Hua Wenqi of Ruzhou acting Jingsheng regent.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛酉，蜀主如武定軍，數日，復還安遠。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xinyou, the Shu ruler went to Wuding Army; after several days he returned again to Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinyou, the Shu ruler visited Wuding. After a few days he was back at Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子朔，蜀主以兼侍中王宗儔為山南節度使、西北面都招討、行營安撫使，天雄節度使、同平章事王宗昱、永寧軍使王宗晏、左神勇軍使王宗信為三招討以副之，將兵伐岐，出故關，壁於咸宜，入良原。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, new moon on wuzi, the Shu ruler made Concurrent Palace Attendant Wang Zongchou Shannan military commissioner, northwest campaign commissioner and field pacification commissioner; Tianxiong military commissioner and associate chief councilor Wang Zongyu, Yongning army commissioner Wang Zongyan, and Left Divine Valor Army commissioner Wang Zongxin the three campaign commissioners as deputies; led troops against Qi, exited the old pass, encamped at Xianyi, and entered Liangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh month's wuzi new moon, the Shu ruler named Wang Zongchou—already palace attendant—Shannan commissioner, northwest campaign commander, and field pacifier, with Wang Zongyu of Tianxiong, Wang Zongyan of Yongning, and Wang Zongxin of the Left Divine Valor Army as his three deputy commanders. They marched against Qi through the old pass, camped at Xianyi, and pushed into Liangyuan.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，王宗儔攻隴州，岐王自將萬五千人屯汧陽。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Wang Zongchou attacked Longzhou; the Prince of Qi personally led fifteen thousand men to encamp at Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Zongchou besieged Longzhou. The Prince of Qi marched in person with fifteen thousand men and held Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，蜀將陳彥威出散關，敗岐兵於箭筈嶺，蜀兵食盡，引還。

translations.literal: On guimao, Shu general Chen Yanwei exited San Pass, defeated Qi troops at Jianhe Ridge; Shu troops' provisions were exhausted and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Chen Yanwei of Shu sallied from San Pass and routed Qi forces at Jianhe Ridge, but supplies ran out and the Shu army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗昱屯秦州，宗儔屯上邽，宗晏、宗信屯威武城。

translations.literal: Zongyu encamped at Qinzhou, Zongchou at Shanggui, Zongyan and Zongxin at Weiwu city.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu held Qinzhou, Zongchou Shanggui, and Zongyan and Zongxin Weiwu city.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，蜀主發安遠城。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Shu ruler departed Anyuan city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Shu ruler left Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，至利州，閬州團練使林思諤來朝，請幸所治，從之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on gengshen, he reached Lizhou; Langzhou regimental commissioner Lin Si'e came to court, requested that he visit his jurisdiction, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, he reached Lizhou. Lin Si'e of Langzhou came to court and invited him to visit his district; the ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，泛江而下，龍舟畫舸，輝映江渚，州縣供辦，民始愁怨。

translations.literal: On guihai he sailed downriver; dragon boats and painted barges glittered along the banks; prefectures and counties supplied his progress, and the people first grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he drifted downriver in dragon boats and painted barges that lit the shores. Every district bore the cost, and popular resentment began.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至閬州，州民何康女色美，將嫁，蜀主取之，賜其夫家帛百匹，夫一慟而卒。

translations.literal: On renshen he reached Langzhou; a daughter of the townsman He Kang was beautiful and about to marry; the Shu ruler took her, gave her betrothed's family a hundred bolts of silk, and the husband died of grief at once.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he reached Langzhou. He Kang's daughter, famed for her beauty, was about to wed when the Shu ruler seized her for the palace, compensated the family with a hundred bolts of silk, and her fiancé died of grief on the spot.

sentences.zh: 癸未，至梓州。

translations.literal: On guiwei he reached Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he arrived at Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 趙王鎔自恃累世鎮成德，得趙人心，生長富貴，雍容自逸，治府第園沼，極一時之盛，多事嬉游，不親政事，事皆仰成於僚佐，深居府第，權移左右，行軍司馬李藹、宦者李弘規用事於中外，宦者石希蒙尤以諂諛得幸。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Yin relied on his house's generations ruling Chengde and winning Zhao hearts; raised in wealth and honor, he was easy and self-indulgent, built mansions and gardens to the utmost splendor of the age, devoted himself to pleasure, did not attend to government, and left affairs to subordinates; dwelling deep in his mansion, power shifted to attendants; marching army marshal Li Ai and eunuch Li Honggui held sway inside and out, and eunuch Shi Ximeng especially won favor through flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin of Zhao trusted that generations of his family had ruled Chengde and won the people's hearts. Raised in luxury, he lived at ease, lavished his estate and gardens until they outshone the age, and chased amusements while leaving government to his staff. Secluded in his mansion, power passed to his intimates—Li Ai as army marshal and Li Honggui the eunuch ruled court and camp alike, while Shi Ximeng curried favor with sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 初，劉仁恭使牙將張文禮從其子守文鎮滄州，守文詣幽州省其父，文禮於後據城作亂，滄人討之，奔鎮州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Rengong had his guard officer Zhang Wenli follow his son Shouwen to garrison Cangzhou; Shouwen went to Youzhou to visit his father; Wenli afterward seized the city in revolt; Cangzhou people attacked him and he fled to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Rengong had sent his guard officer Zhang Wenli to Cangzhou with his son Shouwen. When Shouwen went to Youzhou to see his father, Wenli seized the city in revolt. Cangzhou drove him out and he fled to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 文禮好夸誕，自言知兵，越王鎔奇之，養以為子，更名德明，悉以軍事委之。

translations.literal: Wenli loved boasting and claimed knowledge of warfare; Prince of Yue Yin found him remarkable, adopted him as son, renamed him Deming, and entrusted all military affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli was boastful and called himself a master of war. Prince Yin of Yue took him as an adopted son, renamed him Deming, and handed him the army.

sentences.zh: 德明將行營兵從晉王，鎔欲寄以腹心，使都指揮使符習代還，以為防城使。

translations.literal: Deming led field-army troops with the Prince of Jin; Yin wished to place his trust in him, sent commander-in-chief Fu Xi to replace and return him, and made him city-defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deming led the field army with the Prince of Jin. Yin meant to bind him close, recalled him via Fu Xi, commander-in-chief, and named him city-defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎔晚年好事佛及求仙，專講佛經，受符菉，廣齋醮，合煉仙丹，盛飾館宇於西山，每往游之，登山臨水，數月方歸，將佐士卒陪從者常不下萬人，往來供頓，軍民皆苦之。

translations.literal: In his later years Yin loved Buddhism and seeking immortality, devoted himself to sutras, received talismans, held many fasts and rites, compounded elixirs, lavishly adorned lodges on West Mountain, visited them often, climbed mountains and gazed on waters, returning only after many months; officers and soldiers accompanying him were never fewer than ten thousand; supplies for coming and going burdened army and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: In old age Yin turned to Buddhism and immortality—sutras, talismans, endless fasts, elixir furnaces, and palatial lodges on West Mountain where he lingered for months among peaks and streams. Ten thousand officers and men routinely escorted him, and the cost fell heavily on army and people.

sentences.zh: 是月，自西山還，宿鶻營莊，石希蒙勸王復之它所。

translations.literal: That month, returning from West Mountain, he lodged at Gueying Manor; Shi Ximeng urged the prince to go elsewhere again.
translations.idiomatic: That month, returning from West Mountain, he stayed at Gueying Manor, where Shi Ximeng urged another outing.

sentences.zh: 李弘規言於王曰：「晉王夾河血戰，櫛風沐雨，親冒矢石，而王專以供軍之資奉不急之費，且時方艱難，人心難測，王久虛府第，遠出遊從，萬一有奸人為變，閉關相距，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Li Honggui said to the prince: "The Prince of Jin fights bloody battles along the river, endures wind and rain, personally braves arrows and stones, while Your Highness spends funds meant for the army on needless pleasures; moreover times are hard and hearts unpredictable—Your Highness long absent from the mansion, roaming far—if villains plot revolt and shut the passes against you, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Li Honggui warned the prince, "The Prince of Jin bleeds along the Yellow River, weathers wind and rain, and faces arrows in person—while you spend army funds on pleasure. Times are perilous and hearts fickle. You leave the mansion empty and wander far. If traitors rise and shut the gates, what then?"

sentences.zh: 王將歸，希蒙密言於王曰：「弘規妄生猜間，出不遜語以劫脅王，專欲誇大於外，長威福耳。」

translations.literal: 」The prince was about to return when Ximeng secretly said: "Honggui rashly breeds suspicion, speaks insolently to coerce Your Highness, and only wishes to magnify himself abroad and extend his power.
translations.idiomatic: 」As the prince prepared to return, Ximeng whispered, "Honggui sows suspicion and speaks insolently to bully you—he only wants power abroad."

sentences.zh: 王遂留，信宿無歸志。

translations.literal: 」The prince then stayed; after two nights he still had no mind to return.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince stayed on, and after two nights still would not go home.

sentences.zh: 弘規乃教內牙都將蘇漢衡帥親軍，擐甲拔刃，詣帳前白王曰：「士卒暴露已久，願從王歸！」

translations.literal: Honggui then had inner guard commander Su Hanheng lead the personal guard, don armor and draw blades, come before the tent and report: "The soldiers have long been exposed to the elements—we wish to follow Your Highness home!
translations.idiomatic: Honggui had Su Hanheng, inner guard commander, arm the personal troops, draw swords, and announce at the tent, "The men have suffered long in the open—we beg Your Highness to return home!"

sentences.zh: 弘規因進言曰：「石希蒙勸王游從不已，且聞欲陰謀為逆，請誅之以謝眾。」

translations.literal: 」Honggui then advanced: "Shi Ximeng endlessly urges Your Highness to roam, and it is heard he plots treason in secret—please execute him to appease the masses.
translations.idiomatic: 」Honggui added, "Ximeng keeps urging these outings and is said to plot rebellion—execute him to satisfy the troops."

sentences.zh: 王不聽，牙兵遂大噪，斬希蒙首，訴於前。

translations.literal: 」The prince would not listen; the guard soldiers then raised a great clamor, beheaded Ximeng, and presented the grievance before him.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince refused. The guards roared, cut off Ximeng's head, and laid their grievance before him.

sentences.zh: 王怒且懼，亟歸府。

translations.literal: The prince was angry and afraid and hastened back to the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Furious and afraid, the prince rushed home.

sentences.zh: 是夕，遣其長子副大使昭祚與王德明將兵圍弘規及李靄之第，族誅之，連坐者數十家。

translations.literal: That evening he sent his eldest son Vice Ambassador Zhaozuo and Wang Deming with troops to surround the mansions of Honggui and Li Ai and exterminate their clans; dozens of families were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent his heir Zhaozuo and Wang Deming to surround the houses of Honggui and Li Ai and wipe out their clans—dozens of families implicated.

sentences.zh: 又殺蘇漢衡，收其黨與，窮治反狀，親軍大恐。

translations.literal: He also killed Su Hanheng, seized his partisans, exhaustively investigated sedition, and the personal guard was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Su Hanheng was killed too, his followers rounded up, sedition hunted to the root, and the personal guard was terrified.

sentences.zh: 吳金陵城成，隱彥謙上費用冊籍，徐溫曰：「吾既任公，不復會計！」

translations.literal: Wu's Jinling city wall was completed; Yin Yanqian submitted expense registers; Xu Wen said: "Since I have entrusted it to you, I will no longer keep accounts!
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling's walls were finished in Wu, Yin Yanqian submitted the expense ledgers. Xu Wen said, "I put you in charge—I won't audit the books!"

sentences.zh: 悉焚之。

translations.literal: 」He burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: 」And burned them all.

sentences.zh: 初，閩王審知承製加其從子泉州刺史延彬領平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Min ruler Shenzhi by imperial order added his cousin Quanzhou prefect Yanbin as concurrent Pinglu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Min's Shenzhi had his cousin Yanbin, Quanzhou prefect, also named Pinglu commissioner by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 延彬治泉州十七年，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Yanbin governed Quanzhou seventeen years; officials and people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin ruled Quanzhou seventeen years to general satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 會得白鹿及紫芝，僧浩源以為王者之符，延彬由是驕縱，密遣使浮海入貢，求為泉州節度使。

translations.literal: He obtained a white deer and purple fungus; monk Haoyuan took them as signs of kingship; Yanbin thereby grew arrogant, secretly sent envoys by sea to offer tribute, and sought to be Quanzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When a white deer and purple fungus appeared, monk Haoyuan called them royal omens. Yanbin grew arrogant, sent secret tribute by sea, and asked to be Quanzhou commissioner in his own right.

sentences.zh: 事覺，審知誅浩源及其黨，黜延彬歸私第。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, Shenzhi executed Haoyuan and his faction and demoted Yanbin to private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Exposed, Shenzhi executed Haoyuan and his circle and sent Yanbin home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 漢主巖遣使通好於蜀。

translations.literal: Han ruler Yan sent envoys to open friendly relations with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler Yan sent envoys to court Shu.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐遣使為其子傳琇求婚於楚，楚王殷許之。

translations.literal: Wuyue King Qian Liu sent envoys to seek marriage for his son Chuanyu with Chu; Chu King Yin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue asked Chu for his son Chuanyu's bride; King Yin of Chu consented.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午，蜀主還成都。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiawu, the Shu ruler returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiawu, the Shu ruler returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀主之為太子，高祖為聘兵部尚書高知言女為妃，無寵，及韋妃入宮，尤見疏薄，至是遣還家，知言驚僕，不食而卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shu ruler was heir, the founding emperor betrothed to him the daughter of Minister of Personnel Gao Zhiyan as consort; she had no favor; when Consort Wei entered the palace she was especially neglected; now she was sent home; Zhiyan collapsed in shock and died without eating.
translations.idiomatic: When he had been heir, the founding emperor had matched him with Gao Zhiyan's daughter, Minister of Personnel—but she never won favor. After Lady Wei entered the palace the first consort was cast aside and sent home. Zhiyan collapsed and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 韋妃者，徐耕之孫也，有姝色，蜀主適徐氏，見而悅之，太后因納於後宮，蜀主不欲娶於母族，托雲韋昭度之孫。

translations.literal: Consort Wei was granddaughter of Xu Geng, of striking beauty; the Shu ruler was visiting the Xu house, saw her and was pleased; the empress dowager therefore placed her in the inner palace; the Shu ruler did not wish to marry within his mother's clan and pretended she was granddaughter of Wei Zhaodu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei was Xu Geng's granddaughter, famed for beauty. The Shu ruler saw her on a visit to the Xu house; the empress dowager installed her in the palace. He disliked marrying kin and claimed she was Wei Zhaodu's granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 初為婕妤，累加元妃。

translations.literal: At first she was a talented lady, and was repeatedly promoted to primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: She began as a talented lady and rose to primary consort.

sentences.zh: 蜀主常列錦步障，擊球其中，往往遠適而外人不知，爇諸香，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler often set brocade screens and played ball within them, often going far while outsiders did not know; he burned many incenses day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched brocade screens for polo and slipped away unseen, while incense burned day and night.

sentences.zh: 久而厭之，更爇皁莢以亂其氣。

translations.literal: After long he grew weary and instead burned soap pods to confuse the scents.
translations.idiomatic: In time he tired of perfume and burned soap pods to muddle the air.

sentences.zh: 結繒為山，及宮殿樓觀於其上，或為風雨所敗，則更以新者易之。

translations.literal: He fashioned mountains of silk and palaces and towers upon them; when ruined by wind and rain he replaced them with new ones.
translations.idiomatic: He built silk mountains crowned with palaces; storms destroyed them and he built anew.

sentences.zh: 或樂飲繒山，涉旬不下。

translations.literal: Sometimes he feasted on the silk mountain for more than ten days without descending.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he feasted on the silk mountain ten days without coming down.

sentences.zh: 山前穿渠通禁中，或乘船夜歸，令宮女秉蠟炬千餘居前船，卻立照之，水面如晝。

translations.literal: A canal was cut before the mountain into the forbidden precincts; sometimes he returned by boat at night, ordering palace women to hold more than a thousand wax torches before the leading boat, standing backward to shine on the water so it was bright as day.
translations.idiomatic: A canal linked the mountain to the inner palace. He sometimes rowed home at night with a thousand palace women holding torches astern until the water shone like noon.

sentences.zh: 或酣餘禁中，鼓吹沸騰，以至達旦。

translations.literal: Sometimes drunk within the forbidden precincts, music boiled until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he drank inside until drums and pipes roared till dawn.

sentences.zh: 以是為常。

translations.literal: This became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Such became his habit.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，徙靜勝節度使溫昭圖為匡國節度使，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Jingsheng military commissioner Wen Zhaotu was moved to Kuangguo military commissioner, stationed at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Wen Zhaotu of Jingsheng was transferred to Kuangguo commissioner at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 昭圖素事趙巖，故得名籓。

translations.literal: Zhaotu had long served Zhao Yan and therefore obtained a famous commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotu had long served Zhao Yan and thus won a prestigious post.

sentences.zh: 蜀主、吳主屢以書勸晉王稱帝，晉王以書示僚佐曰：「昔王太師亦嘗遺先王書，勸以唐室已亡，宜自帝一方。

translations.literal: The Shu and Wu rulers repeatedly wrote urging the Prince of Jin to take the imperial title; the prince showed the letters to his staff and said: "Long ago Grand Mentor Wang also sent my late father a letter urging that the Tang house was dead and he should declare himself emperor in one region.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Wu repeatedly urged the Prince of Jin to take the throne. He showed their letters to his staff: "Grand Mentor Wang once told my father the Tang was finished and he should rule alone.

sentences.zh: 先王語余云：『昔天子幸石門，吾發兵誅賊臣，當是之時，威振天下，吾若挾天子據關中，自作九錫禪文，誰能禁我！

translations.literal: My late father told me: 'Long ago when the Son of Heaven visited Shimen, I raised troops to execute treacherous ministers; at that time my might shook the world; if I had seized the Son of Heaven and held Guanzhong, composed the Nine Bestowals and abdication text myself, who could have stopped me!
translations.idiomatic: Father said, 'When the emperor came to Shimen I marched against traitors and awed the realm. I could have held the emperor, seized Guanzhong, and forged the ritual of abdication—who would have stopped me?

sentences.zh: 顧吾家世忠孝，立功帝室，誓死不為耳。

translations.literal: Yet our house for generations has been loyal and filial, establishing merit for the imperial house, and I swore I would not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our house has served the throne in loyalty for generations—I swore never to do it.

sentences.zh: 汝它日當務以復唐社稷為心，慎勿效此曹所為！』

translations.literal: You in future days must take restoring the Tang altars as your heart's aim; beware of imitating such men!'
translations.idiomatic: You must restore the Tang—never imitate those men!

sentences.zh: 言猶在耳，此議非所敢聞也。」

translations.literal: Those words are still in my ears; this proposal is not what I dare hear."
translations.idiomatic: Those words still ring in my ears. I dare not hear this proposal."

sentences.zh: 因泣。

translations.literal: He wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept.

sentences.zh: 既而將佐及蕃鎮勸進不已，乃令有司市玉造法物。

translations.literal: Then his generals and frontier commissioners urged enthronement without cease, and he ordered the offices to purchase jade and make ritual objects.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and frontier lords kept pressing him until he ordered jade and regalia purchased.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之破長安也，魏州僧傳真之師得傳國寶，藏之四十年，至是，傳真以為常玉，將鬻之，或識之，曰：「傳國寶也。」

translations.literal: When Huang Chao broke Chang'an, the teacher of Weizhou monk Chuanzhen obtained the imperial heirloom seal and hid it forty years; now Chuanzhen thought it ordinary jade and meant to sell it; someone recognized it and said: "It is the imperial heirloom seal."
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao sacked Chang'an, Chuanzhen's teacher in Weizhou found the imperial seal and hid it forty years. Chuanzhen meant to sell it as common jade until someone cried, "The imperial seal!

sentences.zh: 傳真乃詣行台獻之，將佐皆奉觴稱賀。

translations.literal: Chuanzhen then went to the field headquarters to present it; the staff all raised cups in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzhen brought it to headquarters; the staff toasted in celebration.

sentences.zh: 張承業在晉陽聞之，詣魏州諫曰：「吾王世世忠於唐室，救其患難，所以老奴三十餘年為王捃拾財賦，召補兵馬，誓滅逆賊，復本朝宗社耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengye at Jinyang heard of it, went to Weizhou and remonstrated: "Our house for generations has been loyal to the Tang, saving it in distress; therefore this old slave for thirty-odd years gathered wealth and levies for Your Highness, recruited and replenished troops and horses, swearing to destroy the rebel bandits and restore the altars of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye at Jinyang heard and hurried to Weizhou: "Our house has served the Tang for generations. I spent thirty years gathering wealth and troops to destroy rebels and restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今河北甫定，朱氏尚存，而王遽即大位，殊非從來征伐之意，天下其誰不解體乎！

translations.literal: Now Hebei is just settled, the Zhu clan still lives, yet Your Highness hastily takes the great throne—this is utterly unlike the intent of campaigns past; who under heaven will not lose heart!
translations.idiomatic: Hebei is barely settled and Zhu still lives—yet you seize the throne? Who will not lose heart?

sentences.zh: 王何不先滅朱氏，復列聖之深仇，然後求唐後而立之，南取吳，西取蜀，汛掃宇內，合為一家，當是之時，雖使高宜、太宗復生，誰敢居王上者？

translations.literal: Why does Your Highness not first destroy the Zhu clan, avenge the deep wrongs of successive emperors, then seek a Tang descendant and enthrone him, take Wu in the south and Shu in the west, sweep the realm and unite it as one house—at that time, even if Gao Yi and Taizong were reborn, who would dare sit above Your Highness?
translations.idiomatic: Destroy Zhu first, avenge the emperors, enthrone a Tang heir, take Wu and Shu, unite the realm—then even if Taizong returned, who would sit above you?

sentences.zh: 讓之愈久則得之愈堅矣。

translations.literal: The longer you yield, the firmer your hold when you take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yield longer and your claim grows firmer.

sentences.zh: 老奴之志無它，但以受先王大恩，欲為王立萬年之基耳。」

translations.literal: This old slave's aim has no other end but, having received the late king's great grace, to establish an enduring foundation for Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: I only wish, for your father's sake, to lay an enduring foundation for you.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「此非余所願，奈群下意何。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "This is not my wish; what can I do about the will of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "It is not my wish—but what can I do against the multitude?

sentences.zh: 承業知不可止，慟哭曰：「諸侯血戰，本為唐家，今王自取之，誤老奴矣！」

translations.literal: Chengye knew it could not be stopped, wept and said: "The feudal lords fought in blood for the Tang house; now Your Highness takes it yourself—you have misled this old slave!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye wept, "Lords bled for the Tang—and you take it yourself. You have misled me!

sentences.zh: 即歸晉陽邑，成疾，不復起。

translations.literal: He returned to his estate at Jinyang, fell ill, and rose no more.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to Jinyang, fell ill, and never rose again.

sentences.zh: 二月，吳改元順義。

translations.literal: Second month, Wu changed the era name to Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wu adopted the era name Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 趙王既殺李弘規、李靄，委政於其子昭祚。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Yin had killed Li Honggui and Li Ai and entrusted government to his son Zhaozuo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin of Zhao, having killed Honggui and Ai, handed rule to his son Zhaozuo.

sentences.zh: 昭祚性驕愎，既得大權，曏時附弘規者皆族之。

translations.literal: Zhaozuo was arrogant and obstinate; once he held great power, he exterminated all who had sided with Honggui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozuo was proud and harsh; he slaughtered everyone who had backed Honggui.

sentences.zh: 弘規部兵五百人欲逃，聚泣偶語，未知所之。

translations.literal: Honggui's five hundred troops wished to flee; they gathered weeping and murmured, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred of Honggui's men gathered to flee, weeping and unsure where to turn.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍有給賜，趙王仇親軍之殺石希蒙，獨不時與，眾益懼。

translations.literal: When the armies were to receive grants, Prince of Zhao Yin, bearing a grudge against the personal guard for killing Shi Ximeng, alone did not issue theirs in time; the masses grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When pay was due, Yin withheld the personal guard's share to punish them for killing Ximeng, and fear spread.

sentences.zh: 王德明素蓄異志，因其懼而激之曰：「王命我盡坑爾曹。

translations.literal: Wang Deming had long harbored other designs; using their fear he incited them: "The prince orders me to slaughter you all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Deming, nursing other ambitions, played on their fear: "The prince orders me to kill you all.

sentences.zh: 吾念爾曹無罪並命，欲從王命則不忍，不然又獲罪於王，奈何？」

translations.literal: I think you guiltless and cannot bear to follow the prince's order, yet if I do not I again offend the prince—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: You are innocent—I cannot obey—yet disobedience offends him. What then?

sentences.zh: 眾皆感泣。

translations.literal: All were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: They wept.

sentences.zh: 是夕，親軍有宿於潭城西門者，相與飲酒而謀之。

translations.literal: That night personal guards lodging west of Tan city gate drank together and plotted.
translations.idiomatic: That night guards at Tan's west gate drank and plotted.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，其中驍健者曰：「吾曹識王太保意，今夕富貴決矣！」

translations.literal: When drunk, the boldest among them said: "We know the intent of Vice Commissioner the prince's son—tonight wealth and rank are decided!"
translations.idiomatic: The boldest drunk cried, "We know the vice commissioner's mind—tonight decides our fortune!

sentences.zh: 即逾城入。

translations.literal: They scaled the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled the wall.

sentences.zh: 趙王方焚香受菉，二人斷其首而出，因焚府第。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao was burning incense receiving talismans when two men cut off his head and came out, then burned the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was receiving talismans when two men struck off his head, burned the mansion, and fled.

sentences.zh: 軍校張友順帥眾詣德明第，請為留後，德明複姓名曰張文禮，盡滅王氏之族，獨置昭祚之妻普寧公主以自托於梁。

translations.literal: Army officer Zhang Youshun led the masses to Deming's house asking him to be regent; Deming restored the name Zhang Wenli, exterminated the Wang clan, and alone kept Zhaozuo's wife Princess Puning to entrust himself to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youshun presented Deming as regent. He took back the name Zhang Wenli, wiped out the Wangs, and kept Princess Puning to court Liang.

sentences.zh: 三月，吳人歸吳越王鏐從弟龍武統軍鎰於錢唐，鏐亦歸吳將李濤於廣陵。

translations.literal: Third month, Wu returned Wuyue King Liu's cousin Longwu commander Yi to Qiantang; Liu also returned Wu general Li Tao to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wu returned Yi to Qiantang; Liu returned Li Tao to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 徐溫以濤為右雄武統軍，鏐以鎰為鎮海節度副使。

translations.literal: Xu Wen made Tao Right Valiant Martial commander; Liu made Yi vice commissioner of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Wen made Tao Right Valiant Martial commander; Liu made Yi Zhenhai vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張文禮遣使告亂於晉王，且奉箋勸進，因求節鉞。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli sent envoys reporting the turmoil to the Prince of Jin and with a memorial urged enthronement, also seeking the seal and axe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli reported to the Prince of Jin, urged enthronement, and sought the commission.

sentences.zh: 晉王方置酒作樂，聞之，投杯悲泣，欲討之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was setting wine and making music when he heard it; he cast aside his cup and wept in grief, wishing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was feasting when news came. He dashed his cup, wept, and meant to march.

sentences.zh: 僚佐以為文禮罪誠大，然吾方與梁爭，不可更立敵於肘腋，宜且從其請以安之。

translations.literal: Staff said Wenli's crime was indeed great, but they were contending with Liang and could not raise another enemy at the elbow; they should for the moment grant his request to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Staff said the crime was grave but Liang was the foe—grant the request for now.

sentences.zh: 王不得已，夏，四月，遣節度判官盧質承製授文禮成德留後。

translations.literal: The prince had no choice; summer, fourth month, he sent circuit judge Lu Zhi with imperial order to appoint Wenli Chengde regent.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, he sent Lu Zhi to name Wenli Chengde regent.

sentences.zh: 陳州刺史惠王友能反，舉兵趣大梁，詔陝州留後霍彥威、宣義節度使王彥章、控鶴指揮使張漢傑將兵討之。

translations.literal: Chenzhou prefect Prince of Hui Zhu Youneng rebelled, raised troops toward Daliang; an edict ordered Shaanzhou regent Huo Yanwei, Xuanyi military commissioner Wang Yanzang, and Cranes commander Zhang Hanjie to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youneng of Chenzhou rebelled and marched on Daliang. Huo Yanwei, Wang Yanzang, and Zhang Hanjie were sent against him.

sentences.zh: 友能至陳留，兵敗，走還陳州，諸軍圍之。

translations.literal: Youneng reached Chenliu, was defeated, fled back to Chenzhou, and the armies besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Chenliu, was beaten, fled to Chenzhou, and was besieged.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌朔，改元。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingxu the new moon, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, bingxu new moon, the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 初，劉鄩與朱友謙為婚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Xun and Zhu Youqian were connected by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun and Zhu Youqian had been linked by marriage.

sentences.zh: 鄩之受詔討友謙也，至陝州，先遣使移書，諭以禍福；

translations.literal: When Xun received the edict to attack Youqian, at Shaanzhou he first sent a letter explaining fortune and calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Xun, ordered to attack Youqian, paused at Shaanzhou to write of consequences;

sentences.zh: 待之月餘，友謙不從，然後進兵。

translations.literal: he waited more than a month; Youqian did not comply, and then he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: waited a month; Youqian refused; then he marched.

sentences.zh: 尹皓、段凝素忌鄩，因譖之於帝曰：「鄩逗遛養寇，俾俟援兵。」

translations.literal: Yin Hao and Duan Ning had always envied Xun and slandered him to the Emperor: "Xun dallies and nurtures the bandit, waiting for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao and Duan Ning slandered him: "Xun coddles the rebel awaiting Jin aid.

sentences.zh: 帝信之。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor believed it.

sentences.zh: 鄩既敗歸，以疾請解兵柄，詔聽於西都就醫，密令留守張宗奭鴆之，丁亥，卒。

translations.literal: Xun, defeated, returned and asked leave of military command on grounds of illness; an edict allowed him to seek medical care in the western capital; secretly the western capital regent Zhang Zongshi was ordered to poison him; on dinghai he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, defeated, asked to resign for illness. The court sent him to the western capital where Zhang Zongshi poisoned him on dinghai.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on yimao the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, yimao new moon: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，惠王友能降。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Prince of Hui Zhu Youneng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month: Youneng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔赦其死，降封房陵侯。

translations.literal: On gengzi an edict pardoned his death and demoted him to Marquis of Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he was spared death and made Marquis of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 晉王既許籓鎮之請，求唐舊臣，欲以備百官。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, having granted the frontier commissioners' requests, sought old Tang officials to fill the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Having indulged the frontier lords, the prince sought old Tang officials for his court.

sentences.zh: 朱友謙遣前禮部尚書蘇循詣行台，循至魏州，入牙城，望府廨即拜，謂之拜殿。

translations.literal: Former Minister of Rites Su Xun came to the field headquarters; reaching Weizhou he entered the ya gate, saw the government offices and at once bowed, calling it bowing to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister of Rites Su Xun arrived at headquarters. At Weizhou he entered the ya gate, saw the offices, and prostrated himself—calling it "bowing to the hall."

sentences.zh: 見王呼萬歲舞蹈，泣而稱臣。

translations.literal: Seeing the prince he shouted "Long live!" danced, wept, and called himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: Before the prince he shouted "Long live!", danced, wept, and styled himself a subject.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又獻大筆三十枚，謂之「畫日筆」。

translations.literal: The next day he again presented thirty large brushes, calling them "day-painting brushes."
translations.idiomatic: Next day he offered thirty large brushes as "day-painting brushes."

sentences.zh: 王大喜，即命循以本官為河東節度副使，張承業深惡之。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and at once appointed Xun to his former office as Hezhong vice military commissioner; Zhang Chengye deeply detested him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted and named Xun Hezhong vice commissioner at his old rank. Zhang Chengye loathed him.

sentences.zh: 張文禮雖受晉命，內不自安，復遣間使因盧文進求援於契丹；

translations.literal: Though Zhang Wenli accepted Jin appointment, inwardly he was uneasy and again sent secret envoys through Lu Wenjin to seek aid from Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: Though Wenli held Jin's commission, he sent secret envoys via Lu Wenjin to Khitan;

sentences.zh: 又遣間使來告曰：「王氏為亂兵所屠，公主無恙。

translations.literal: he also sent secret envoys reporting: "The Wang house was slaughtered by mutinous soldiers; the princess is unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: another message: "Mutineers butchered the Wangs; the princess is safe.

sentences.zh: 臣已北召契丹，乞朝廷發精甲萬人相助，自德、棣渡河，則晉人遁逃不暇矣。」

translations.literal: I have already summoned Khitan from the north; I beg the court to send ten thousand elite troops to help, crossing from De and Di—then the Jin will have no leisure to flee.
translations.idiomatic: I have summoned Khitan; send ten thousand elites from De and Di—the Jin will not escape."

sentences.zh: 帝疑未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor hesitated undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 敬翔曰：「陛下不乘此釁以復河北，則晉人不可復破矣。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang said: "Your Majesty, if you do not seize this opening to recover Hebei, the Jin can never be broken again.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang urged, "Miss this chance to recover Hebei and Jin will never break.

sentences.zh: 宜徇其請，不可失也。」

translations.literal: You should follow his request; it must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Grant his plea—do not lose it."

sentences.zh: 趙、張輩皆曰：「今強寇近在河上，盡吾兵力以拒之，猶懼不支，何暇分萬人以救張文禮乎！

translations.literal: Zhao and Zhang and the rest all said: "The strong foe is now on the river; we expend all our strength to resist and still fear we cannot hold—how have leisure to divide ten thousand men to save Zhang Wenli!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Zhang objected: "The foe is on the river—we barely hold—how spare ten thousand for Wenli!

sentences.zh: 且文禮坐持兩端，欲以自固，於我何利焉！」

translations.literal: Moreover Wenli sits on two sides to secure himself—what profit for us!
translations.idiomatic: Wenli plays both sides—what gain for us!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 晉人屢於塞上及河津獲文禮蠟丸絹書，晉王皆遣使歸之，文禮慚懼。

translations.literal: Jin forces repeatedly on the frontier and river crossings captured Wenli's wax balls and silk letters; the Prince of Jin always sent envoys to return them; Wenli was ashamed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jin repeatedly captured Wenli's secret letters and returned them; Wenli grew ashamed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 文禮忌趙故將，多所誅滅。

translations.literal: Wenli resented old Zhao generals and executed many.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli killed many old Zhao officers.

sentences.zh: 符習將趙兵萬人從晉王在德勝，文禮請召歸，以它將代之，且以習子蒙為都督府參軍，遣人繼錢帛勞行營將士以悅之。

translations.literal: Fu Xi led ten thousand Zhao troops with the Prince of Jin at Desheng; Wenli asked to recall him, replace him with another general, and made Xi's son Meng staff officer of the headquarters, sending men with continued money and cloth to please field-camp officers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi led ten thousand Zhao troops at Desheng. Wenli recalled him, sent gifts to camp officers, and made Xi's son Meng headquarters staff officer.

sentences.zh: 習見晉王，泣涕請留，晉王曰：「吾與趙王同盟討賊，義猶骨肉，不意一旦禍生肘腋，吾誠痛之。

translations.literal: Xi saw the Prince of Jin, wept and begged to remain; the prince said: "I and Prince of Zhao were allied to attack bandits, close as kin; I did not expect sudden calamity at the elbow—I truly grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wept before the prince, who said, "Prince Yin and I were brothers in arms—I grieve this treachery.

sentences.zh: 汝苟不忘舊君，能為之復仇乎？

translations.literal: If you do not forget your old lord, can you avenge him?
translations.idiomatic: Will you avenge him?

sentences.zh: 吾以兵糧助汝。」

translations.literal: I will aid you with troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: I will give troops and grain."

sentences.zh: 習與部將三十餘人舉身投地慟哭曰：「故使授習等劍，使之攘除寇敵。

translations.literal: Xi and more than thirty subordinate officers threw themselves to the ground weeping: "The late lord gave us swords to drive off enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and thirty officers prostrated themselves: "Our lord gave us swords against enemies.

sentences.zh: 自聞變故以來，冤憤無訴，欲引劍自剄，顧無益於死者，今大王念故使輔佐之勤，許之復冤，習等不敢煩霸府之兵，願以所部徑前搏取凶豎，以報王氏累世之恩，死不恨矣！」

translations.literal: Since we heard of the calamity we have had no outlet for our grievance and wished to draw our swords and cut our throats, but it would not benefit the dead; now Your Highness remembers the late lord's supporting toil and grants revenge—we dare not trouble the headquarters' army; we wish to lead our own troops straight forward to seize the villain and repay the Wang house's generations of grace—we will not regret death!
translations.idiomatic: Since the slaughter we have burned for vengeance. Grant us our own troops—we need no headquarters army—to seize the villain and repay the Wangs, though we die!"

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，晉王以習為成德留後，又命天平節度使閻寶、相州刺史史建瑭將兵助之，自邢洺而北。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on gengshen, the Prince of Jin made Xi Chengde regent, also ordered Tianping military commissioner Yan Bao and Xiangzhou prefect Shi Jianya with troops to help, advancing north from Xing and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the prince named Xi Chengde regent and sent Yan Bao and Shi Jianya north from Xing and Mo.

sentences.zh: 文禮先病腹疽；

translations.literal: Wenli had earlier been ill with an abdominal abscess;
translations.idiomatic: Wenli already suffered an abdominal abscess;

sentences.zh: 甲子，晉兵拔趙州，刺史王鋌降，晉王復以為刺史，文禮聞之，驚懼而卒。

translations.literal: on jiazi Jin troops took Zhaozhou; prefect Wang Kun surrendered; the prince reappointed him prefect; Wenli heard it, was alarmed and afraid and died.
translations.idiomatic: on jiazi Jin took Zhaozhou; Wang Kun surrendered and was reappointed; Wenli heard, panicked, and died.

sentences.zh: 其子處瑾秘不發喪，與其黨韓正時謀悉力拒晉。

translations.literal: His son Chujin concealed the death and with his faction Han Zhengshi plotted to resist Jin with all strength.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chujin hid the death; with Han Zhengshi he resolved to resist.

sentences.zh: 九月，晉兵渡滹沱，圍鎮州，決漕渠以灌之，獲其深州刺史張友順。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Jin troops crossed the Hutuo, besieged Zhenzhou, cut the canal to flood it, and captured its Shenzhou prefect Zhang Youshun.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Jin crossed the Hutuo, besieged Zhenzhou, flooded it by canal, and took Zhang Youshun of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，史建瑭中流矢卒。

translations.literal: On renchen Shi Jianya died of an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Shi Jianya died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 晉王欲自分兵攻鎮州，北面招討使戴思遠聞之，謀悉楊村之眾襲德勝北城，晉王得梁降者，知之，冬，十月，己未，晉王命李嗣源伏兵於戚城，李存審屯德勝，先以騎兵誘之，偽示羸怯。

translations.literal: The prince wished to divide troops to attack Zhenzhou; northern campaign commissioner Dai Siyuan heard it and plotted to strike Desheng's north city with all Yangcun forces; the prince learned from a Liang defector; winter, tenth month, on jiwei he ordered Li Sizhao to ambush at Qicheng and Li Cunshen to hold Desheng, first sending cavalry to lure them, feigning weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan meant to hit Desheng's north wall. On jiwei the prince set Li Sizhao in ambush at Qicheng and Li Cunshen at Desheng, luring Liang with a feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 梁兵競進，晉王嚴中軍以待之；

translations.literal: Liang troops rushed forward; the prince waited in the central army;
translations.idiomatic: Liang charged; the prince held the center;

sentences.zh: 梁兵至，晉王以鐵騎三千奮擊，梁兵大敗，思遠走趣楊村，士卒為晉兵所殺傷及自相蹈藉、墜河陷冰，失亡二萬餘人。

translations.literal: when Liang arrived the prince struck with three thousand iron cavalry; Liang suffered great defeat; Siyuan fled toward Yangcun; soldiers were killed and wounded by Jin troops and by trampling one another, falling into rivers and ice, losing more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: three thousand iron cavalry shattered them; twenty thousand Liang dead or lost.

sentences.zh: 晉王以李嗣源為蕃漢內外馬步副總管、同平章事。

translations.literal: The prince made Li Sizhao vice commander of inner and outer Han and tribal horse and foot and associate chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao became vice commander of all horse and foot and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，義武節度使兼中書令王處直未有子，妖人李應之得小兒劉雲郎於陘邑，以遺處直曰：「是兒有貴相。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Yiwu military commissioner and chief councilor Wang Chuzhi had no sons; a sorcerer Li Yingzhi obtained the boy Liu Yunlang from Lingyi and gave him to Chuzhi saying: "This child has a noble countenance."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu had no sons. Sorcerer Li Yingzhi gave him Liu Yunlang from Lingyi as "noble of countenance."

sentences.zh: 使養為子，名之曰都。

translations.literal: He was raised as son and named Du.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi adopted him as Du.

sentences.zh: 及壯，便佞多詐，處直愛之，置新軍，使典之。

translations.literal: When grown he was clever and deceitful; Chuzhi loved him and established a new army under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, Du was sly and commanded a new army.

sentences.zh: 處直有孽子郁，無寵，奔晉，晉王克用以女妻之，累遷至新州團練使。

translations.literal: Chuzhi had a illegitimate son Yu, unloved, who fled to Jin; Prince of Jin Keyong married him a daughter and promoted him to Xizhou regimental commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Illegitimate son Yu fled to Jin, married Keyong's daughter, and became Xizhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 餘子皆幼；

translations.literal: The other sons were all young;
translations.idiomatic: Other sons were young;

sentences.zh: 處直以都為節度副大使，欲以為嗣。

translations.literal: Chuzhi made Du vice military commissioner intending him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi made Du vice commissioner and heir.

sentences.zh: 及晉王存勖討張文禮，處直以平日鎮、定相為脣齒，恐鎮亡而定孤，固諫，以為方御梁寇，且宜赦文禮。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Cunxu attacked Zhang Wenli, Chuzhi, since Zhen and Ding had long been lip and teeth, feared that if Zhen perished Ding would stand alone, and strongly remonstrated that while resisting Liang they should pardon Wenli.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi warned Cunxu: Zhen and Ding were allies—pardon Wenli while fighting Liang.

sentences.zh: 晉王答以文禮弒君，義不可赦；

translations.literal: The prince answered that Wenli murdered his lord and could not be pardoned on principle;
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused: regicide cannot be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 又潛引梁兵，恐於易定亦不利。

translations.literal: he also secretly brought Liang troops, which would harm Yiding as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli also courts Liang—bad for Yiding.

sentences.zh: 處直患之，以新州地鄰契丹，乃潛遣人語郁，使賂契丹，召令犯塞，務以解鎮州之圍；

translations.literal: Chuzhi was troubled; since Xizhou bordered Khitan he secretly sent word to Yu to bribe Khitan and call them to raid the frontier to relieve Zhenzhou's siege;
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi secretly urged Yu to bribe Khitan to raid and relieve Zhenzhou;

sentences.zh: 其將佐多諫，不聽。

translations.literal: his staff mostly remonstrated; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: staff objected; he ignored them.

sentences.zh: 郁素疾都冒繼其宗，乃邀處直求為嗣，處直許之。

translations.literal: Yu had long resented Du usurping the clan seat and therefore asked Chuzhi to make him heir; Chuzhi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu hated Du and asked to be heir; Chuzhi agreed.

sentences.zh: 軍府之人皆不欲召契丹，都亦慮郁奪其處，乃陰與書吏和昭訓謀劫處直。

translations.literal: The military staff did not wish to summon Khitan; Du also feared Yu seizing his place, and secretly with clerk He Zhaoxun plotted to seize Chuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Officers opposed Khitan; Du and clerk He Zhaoxun plotted a coup.

sentences.zh: 會處直與張文禮使者宴於城東，暮歸，都以新軍數百伏於府第，大噪劫之，曰：「將士不欲以城召契丹，請令公歸西第。」

translations.literal: When Chuzhi was feasting with Zhang Wenli's envoy east of the city and returned at dusk, Du led several hundred of the new army hidden at the mansion, raised a great clamor and seized him, saying: "The soldiers do not wish the city summon Khitan—please let the lord retire to the western residence."
