translations.idiomatic: At dusk Du's new guard seized Chuzhi: "We will not summon Khitan—retire to the west wing."

sentences.zh: 乃並其妻妾幽之西第，盡殺處直子孫在中山及將佐之為處直腹心者。

translations.literal: They imprisoned him with wife and concubines in the western residence and killed all Chuzhi's sons and grandchildren in Zhongshan and staff who were his trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: They jailed him westward and slaughtered his kin and trusted men in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 都自為留後，具以狀白晉王。

translations.literal: Du made himself regent and reported fully to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Du made himself regent and reported to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉王因以都代處直。

translations.literal: The prince therefore replaced Chuzhi with Du.
translations.idiomatic: The prince accepted Du in Chuzhi's place.

sentences.zh: 吳徐溫勸吳王祀南郊，或曰：「禮樂未備且唐祀南郊，其費巨萬，今未能辦也。」

translations.literal: Wu Xu Wen urged the Wu king to sacrifice to Heaven at the southern suburb; some said: "Rites and music are not ready, and when Tang sacrificed at the southern suburb the expense was vast—this cannot yet be done."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen urged a southern suburb rite; critics cited Tang's ruinous expense.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「安有王者而不事天乎！

translations.literal: Wen said: "How can there be a king who does not serve Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "What king does not serve Heaven!

sentences.zh: 吾聞事天貴誠，多費何為！

translations.literal: I hear serving Heaven values sincerity—what need of great expense!
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity, not expense, is what matters!

sentences.zh: 唐每郊祀，啟南門，灌其樞用脂百斛。

translations.literal: Each time Tang sacrificed at the suburb they opened the south gate and greased the pivots with a hundred hu of fat.
translations.idiomatic: Tang greased gate pivots with a hundred hu of fat—

sentences.zh: 此乃季世奢泰之弊，又安足法乎！」

translations.literal: This is the decadent luxury of a declining age—how can it be taken as model!
translations.idiomatic: decadence of a dying age, not a model!"

sentences.zh: 甲子，吳王祀南郊，配以太祖。

translations.literal: On jiazi the Wu king sacrificed at the southern suburb, with the founding emperor as associate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Wu king sacrificed at the southern suburb with the founder.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，大赦；

translations.literal: On yichou there was a great amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou: great amnesty;

sentences.zh: 加徐知誥同平章事，領江州觀察使。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao was added associate chief councilor and Jiangzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao became associate chief councilor and Jiangzhou observer.

sentences.zh: 尋以江州為奉化軍，以知誥領節度使。

translations.literal: Soon Jiangzhou was made Fenghua Army and Zhigao was made its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou became Fenghua Army under Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 徐溫聞壽州團練使崔太初苛察失民心，欲征之，徐知誥曰：「壽州邊隅大鎮，征之恐為變，不若使其入朝，因留之。」

translations.literal: Xu Wen heard Shouzhou regimental commissioner Cui Taichu was harsh and lost popular hearts and wished to summon him; Xu Zhigao said: "Shouzhou is a great border fortress—attacking may cause revolt; better have him enter court and detain him."
translations.idiomatic: Wen meant to punish harsh Cui Taichu of Shouzhou; Zhigao said summon him to court instead.

sentences.zh: 溫怒曰：「一崔太初不能制，如他人何！」

translations.literal: Wen angrily said: "If one Cui Taichu cannot be controlled, what of others!
translations.idiomatic: Wen snapped, "If I cannot control Cui Taichu, what of others!"

sentences.zh: 征為右雄武大將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Valiant Martial general.
translations.idiomatic: Cui was made Right Valiant Martial general.

sentences.zh: 十一月，晉王使李存審、李嗣源守德勝，自將兵攻鎮州。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, the Prince of Jin sent Li Cunshen and Li Sizhao to hold Desheng and personally led troops to attack Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Cunshen and Sizhao held Desheng; the prince besieged Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 張處瑾遣其弟處琪、幕僚齊儉謝罪請服，晉王不許，盡銳攻之，旬日不克。

translations.literal: Zhang Chujin sent his brother Chuji and staff Qi Jian to apologize and submit; the prince did not permit and attacked with full vigor; ten days did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Chujin sent Chuji and Qi Jian to submit; the prince refused and assaulted ten days without success.

sentences.zh: 處瑾使韓正時將千騎突圍出，趣定州，欲求救於王處直。

translations.literal: Chujin sent Han Zhengshi with a thousand horsemen to break out toward Dingzhou to beg Wang Chuzhi for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chujin sent Han Zhengshi with a thousand horse toward Dingzhou for aid.

sentences.zh: 晉兵追至行唐，斬之。

translations.literal: Jin troops pursued to Xingtang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin caught him at Xingtang and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主既許盧文進出兵，王郁又說之曰：「鎮州美女如雲，金帛如山，天皇王速往，則皆己物也，不然，為晉王所有矣。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler, having promised Lu Wenjin troops, and Wang Yu also persuaded him: "Zhenzhou's beauties are like clouds, gold and silk like mountains—Great Heavenly King, go quickly and they are all yours; otherwise the Prince of Jin will have them."
translations.idiomatic: Khitan, promised by Lu Wenjin, was urged by Wang Yu: "Zhenzhou's wealth is yours—hurry or Jin takes it."

sentences.zh: 契丹主以為然，悉發所有之眾而南。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler thought it so and sent all his forces south.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler marched south with all his forces.

sentences.zh: 述律-{后}-諫曰：「吾有西樓羊馬之富，其樂不可勝窮也，何必勞師遠山以乘危徼利乎！

translations.literal: Shulü-{后}- remonstrated: "We have the riches of the western tower sheep and horses, joy beyond counting—why weary the army over distant mountains for perilous profit!
translations.idiomatic: Shulü remonstrated against the risky southern march.

sentences.zh: 吾聞晉王用兵，天下莫敵，脫有危敗，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: I hear the Prince of Jin uses troops and none under heaven can match; if there is perilous defeat, how regret!
translations.idiomatic: She warned of the Prince of Jin's invincibility.

sentences.zh: 契丹主不聽，十二月，辛未，攻幽州，李紹宏嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler did not listen; twelfth month, on xinwei, he attacked Youzhou; Li Shaohong held the city and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored her; twelfth month, xinwei: Khitan attacked Youzhou; Li Shaohong defended.

sentences.zh: 契丹長驅而南，圍涿州，旬日拔之，擒刺史李嗣弼。

translations.literal: Khitan drove south, besieged Zhuozhou, took it in ten days, and captured prefect Li Sibi.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan took Zhuozhou in ten days and captured Li Sibi.

sentences.zh: 進攻定州，王都告急於晉，晉王自鎮州將親軍五千救之，遣神武都指揮使王思同將兵戍狼山之南以拒之。

translations.literal: They advanced on Dingzhou; Wang Du urgently reported to Jin; the prince led five thousand of his personal guard to rescue, sent Divine Martial commander Wang Sitong with troops to guard south of Langshan to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan besieged Dingzhou; the prince led five thousand to rescue; Wang Sitong guarded Langshan.

sentences.zh: 高季昌遣都指揮使倪可福以卒萬人修江陵外郭，季昌行視，責功程之慢，杖之。

translations.literal: Gao Jichang sent commander Ni Kefu with ten thousand men to repair Jiangling's outer wall; Jichang inspected and punished slow work with the cane.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jichang sent Ni Kefu to repair Jiangling's walls and beat slow workers.

sentences.zh: 季昌女為可福子知進婦，季昌謂其女曰：「歸語汝舅：吾欲威眾辦事耳。」

translations.literal: Jichang's daughter was wife to Kefu's son Zhijin; Jichang told her: "Tell your uncle: I wished only to awe the masses and hurry the work."
translations.idiomatic: He told his daughter to reassure Kefu he only meant to hurry the work.

sentences.zh: 以白金數百兩遺之。

translations.literal: He gave several hundred taels of white gold in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent hundreds of taels of white gold in compensation.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢以尚書左丞倪曙同平章事。

translations.literal: That year Han made Secretariat Left Assistant Director Ni Shu associate chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That year Han made Ni Shu associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 辰、漵蠻侵楚，楚寧遠節度副使姚彥章討平之。

translations.literal: Chen and Xu barbarians raided Chu; Chu Ningyuan vice commissioner Yao Yanzhang pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Xu tribes raided Chu; Yao Yanzhang pacified them.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午朔，王都省王處直於西第，處直奮拳毆其胸，曰：「逆賊，我何負於汝！」

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on renwu the new moon, Wang Du visited Wang Chuzhi in the western residence; Chuzhi struck his chest with his fist: "Rebel—what have I failed to give you!
translations.idiomatic: Spring, renwu new moon: Du visited Chuzhi, who struck his chest crying "Traitor—what did I owe you!

sentences.zh: 既無兵刃，將噬其鼻，都掣袂獲免。

translations.literal: Having no weapon he tried to bite his nose; Du pulled his sleeve and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Unarmed, Chuzhi tried to bite his nose; Du fled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，處直憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Before long Chuzhi died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chuzhi died of grief.

sentences.zh: 甲午，晉王至新城南，候騎白契丹前鋒宿新樂，涉沙河而南；

translations.literal: On jiawu the prince reached south of Xincheng; scouts reported Khitan vanguard encamped at Xinle, crossing the Sha River south;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the prince reached Xincheng; scouts reported Khitan at Xinle crossing the Sha south;

sentences.zh: 將士皆失色，士卒有亡去者，主將斬之不能止。

translations.literal: officers and soldiers all lost color; soldiers fled and commanders beheaded them but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: troops panicked and fled despite executions.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「虜傾國而來，吾眾寡不敵；

translations.literal: All generals said: "The barbarians have come with the whole nation; our numbers cannot match;
translations.idiomatic: Generals urged retreat: "We are outnumbered;

sentences.zh: 又聞梁寇內侵，宜且還師魏州以救根本，或請釋鎮州之圍，西入井陘避之。」

translations.literal: moreover we hear Liang invades within—better return to Weizhou to save the root, or lift the Zhenzhou siege and enter Jingxing Pass to avoid them."
translations.idiomatic: Liang threatens within—return to Weizhou or lift the siege."

sentences.zh: 晉王猶豫未決，中門使郭崇韜曰：「契丹為王郁所誘，本利貨財而來，非能救鎮州之急難也。

translations.literal: The prince still hesitated; inner-gate officer Guo Chongtao said: "Khitan was lured by Wang Yu for goods, not to save Zhenzhou's crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao said Khitan came for loot, not Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王新破梁兵，威振夷、夏，契丹聞王至，心沮氣索，苟挫其前鋒，遁走必矣。」

translations.literal: Your Highness has newly broken Liang troops and awed Yi and Xia; when Khitan hear you have come their hearts will be discouraged and breath short—if we break their vanguard they will surely flee."
translations.idiomatic: Break their vanguard and they flee."

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭自潞州至，亦曰：「今強敵在前，吾有進無退，不可輕動以搖人心。」

translations.literal: Li Sizhao arrived from Luzhou and also said: "With a strong foe before us we advance, never retreat—do not lightly shake hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao from Luzhou said advance, never retreat.

sentences.zh: 晉王曰：「帝王之興，自有天命，契丹其如我何！

translations.literal: The prince said: "The rise of emperors has its own mandate—what can Khitan do to me!
translations.idiomatic: The prince said emperors rise by mandate—Khitan cannot harm him.

sentences.zh: 吾以數萬之眾平定山東，今遇此小虜而避之，何面目以臨四海！」

translations.literal: With my tens of thousands I pacified Shandong—how face the realm if I avoid this small barbarian!
translations.idiomatic: How face the realm fleeing a small foe!

sentences.zh: 乃自帥鐵騎五千先進。

translations.literal: He then personally led five thousand iron cavalry forward first.
translations.idiomatic: He led five thousand iron cavalry forward.

sentences.zh: 至新城北，半出桑林，契丹萬餘騎見之，驚走。

translations.literal: North of Xincheng, half out of mulberry groves, more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen saw them and fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: North of Xincheng ten thousand Khitan horsemen fled at sight of him.

sentences.zh: 晉王分軍為二逐之，行數十里，獲契丹主之子。

translations.literal: The prince divided the army in two to pursue; after many li they captured the Khitan ruler's son.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and captured the Khitan ruler's son.

sentences.zh: 時沙河橋狹冰薄，契丹陷溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The Sha River bridge was narrow with thin ice; Khitan drowned in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Thin ice on the Sha drowned many Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是夕，晉王宿新樂。

translations.literal: That evening the prince lodged at Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: That night he camped at Xinle.

sentences.zh: 契丹主車帳在定州城下，敗兵至，契丹舉眾退保望都。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler's cart and tent were below Dingzhou city; defeated troops arrived and Khitan withdrew to hold Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan withdrew to Wangdu after defeat.

sentences.zh: 晉王至定州，王都迎謁於馬前，宴於府第，請以愛女妻王子繼岌。

translations.literal: The prince reached Dingzhou; Wang Du met him before his horse, feasted at the mansion, and asked to give his beloved daughter to the prince's son Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou Wang Du feasted him and offered his daughter to Jiji.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，晉王引兵趣望都，契丹逆戰，晉王以親軍千騎先進，遇奚酋禿餒五千騎，為其所圍。

translations.literal: On wuxu the prince led troops toward Wangdu; Khitan met in battle; the prince sent a thousand personal guard cavalry ahead and met Xi chief Tuluwi's five thousand horsemen and was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Khitan fought; a thousand guard cavalry met Tuluwi's five thousand and were surrounded.

sentences.zh: 晉王力戰，出入數四，自午至申不解。

translations.literal: The prince fought fiercely, entering and leaving four or five times, from noon to shen without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The prince fought from noon to shen, trapped four or five times.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭聞之，引三百騎橫擊之，虜退，王乃得出。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao heard it and led three hundred horsemen to strike across; the barbarians retreated and the prince emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao's three hundred broke the ring and freed him.

sentences.zh: 因縱兵奮擊，契丹大敗，逐北至易州。

translations.literal: Then he loosed troops in fierce pursuit; Khitan suffered great defeat and was pursued north to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursued to Yizhou in great victory.

sentences.zh: 會大雪彌旬，平地數尺，契丹人馬無食，死者相屬於道。

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell for more than ten days; on level ground several chi; Khitan men and horses had no food; the dead lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell ten days; Khitan men and horses starved; corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 契丹主舉手指天，謂盧文進曰：「天未令我至此。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler pointed at heaven and said to Lu Wenjin: "Heaven did not wish me to come here."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler told Lu Wenjin, "Heaven did not mean me to come."

sentences.zh: 乃北歸。

translations.literal: He then returned north.
translations.idiomatic: He marched north.

sentences.zh: 晉王引兵躡之，隨其行止，見其野宿之所，布蒿於地，迴環方正，皆如編剪，雖去，無一枝亂者，歎曰：「虜用法嚴乃能如是，中國所不及也。」

translations.literal: The prince followed; wherever they camped in the wild they laid artemisia on the ground in square rings neat as if cut with scissors; though they left, not one twig was disordered; he sighed: "The barbarians' discipline is strict to be thus—China cannot match it."
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing, he admired Khitan camp discipline—artemisia squares perfect as cut cloth.

sentences.zh: 晉王至幽州，使二百騎躡契丹之後，曰：「虜出境即還。」

translations.literal: The prince reached Youzhou and sent two hundred horsemen to trail Khitan, saying: "When the barbarians leave the border then return."
translations.idiomatic: At Youzhou he sent two hundred horse to shadow Khitan until they crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 騎恃勇追擊之，悉為所擒，惟兩騎自它道走免。

translations.literal: The horsemen relied on courage in pursuit and were all captured; only two horsemen escaped by another road.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers were captured; only two escaped.

sentences.zh: 契丹主責王郁，縶之以歸，自是不聽其謀。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler blamed Wang Yu, bound him and took him back; from then on he did not heed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan blamed Wang Yu, bound him, and ignored his counsel thereafter.

sentences.zh: 晉代州刺史李嗣肱將兵定媯、儒、武等州，授山北都團練使。

translations.literal: Jin Daizhou prefect Li Sigong led troops to pacify Gui, Ru, Wu and other prefectures and was appointed commander of the northern mountains regiments.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sigong of Daizhou pacified northern prefectures and became mountain regiments commander.

sentences.zh: 晉王之北攻鎮州也，李存審謂李嗣源曰：「梁人聞我在南兵少，不攻德勝，必襲魏州。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin marched north to attack Zhenzhou, Li Cunshen said to Li Sizhao: "Liang hear we are few in the south and will not attack Desheng but will strike Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen warned Sizhao: Liang may strike Weizhou while we are few in the south.

sentences.zh: 吾二人聚於此何為！

translations.literal: What are we two gathered here for!
translations.idiomatic: Why stay here together!

sentences.zh: 不若分軍備之。」

translations.literal: Better divide troops to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Split forces to guard.

sentences.zh: 遂分軍屯澶州。

translations.literal: They then divided troops to encamp at Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They camped detachments at Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戴思遠果悉楊村之眾趣魏州，嗣源引兵先之，軍於狄公祠下，遣人告魏州，使為之備。

translations.literal: Dai Siyuan indeed led all Yangcun forces toward Weizhou; Sizhao led troops ahead first and encamped below the Di Gong shrine, sending men to warn Weizhou to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan marched on Weizhou; Sizhao camped at the Di Gong shrine and warned Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 思遠至魏店，嗣源遣其將石萬全將騎兵挑戰。

translations.literal: Siyuan reached Weidian; Sizhao sent his officer Shi Wanquan with cavalry to challenge.
translations.idiomatic: At Weidian Sizhao's Shi Wanquan challenged him.

sentences.zh: 思遠知有備，乃西渡洹水，拔成安，大掠而還。

translations.literal: Siyuan knew there was preparation and crossed the Huan River west, took Cheng'an, and plundered greatly on return.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan crossed west, sacked Cheng'an, and withdrew looting.

sentences.zh: 又將兵五萬攻德勝北城，重塹復壘，斷其出入，晝夜急攻之，李存審悉力拒守。

translations.literal: He again led fifty thousand troops to attack Desheng's north city, rebuilt trenches and ramparts, cut off entry and exit, and attacked day and night; Li Cunshen resisted with all strength.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Desheng's north wall with fifty thousand; Cunshen held.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞德勝勢危，二月，自幽州赴之，五日至魏州。

translations.literal: The prince heard Desheng was in peril; second month, from Youzhou he hastened there, reaching Weizhou in five days.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Desheng's peril, the prince rode from Youzhou in five days.

sentences.zh: 思遠聞之，燒營遁還楊村。

translations.literal: Siyuan heard it, burned camp and fled back to Yangcun.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan burned camp and fled to Yangcun.

sentences.zh: 蜀主好為微行，酒肆、倡家靡所不到，惡人識之，乃下令士民皆著大裁帽。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler loved to travel incognito; wine shops and singing houses he did not miss; fearing recognition he ordered civil and military all to wear large-brimmed hats.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler roamed in disguise and made everyone wear large hats to hide him.

sentences.zh: 晉天平節度使兼侍中閻寶築壘以圍鎮州，決滹沱水環之。

translations.literal: Jin Tianping military commissioner and palace attendant Yan Bao built fortifications to besiege Zhenzhou and cut the Hutuo to ring it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao of Tianping besieged Zhenzhou and ringed it with the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 內外斷絕，城中食盡。

translations.literal: Inside and outside were cut off; food in the city was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The city was starved and cut off.

sentences.zh: 丙午，遣五百餘人出求食。

translations.literal: On bingwu more than five hundred men went out to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu five hundred went out for food.

sentences.zh: 寶縱其出，欲伏兵取之；

translations.literal: Bao let them out intending to ambush;
translations.idiomatic: Bao meant to ambush them;

sentences.zh: 其人遂攻長圍，寶輕之，不為備，俄數千人繼至。

translations.literal: they instead attacked the long encirclement; Bao underestimated them and was unprepared; soon several thousand followed.
translations.idiomatic: they attacked the siege lines; thousands followed.

sentences.zh: 諸軍未集，鎮人遂壞長圍而出，縱火攻寶營，寶不能拒，退保趙州。

translations.literal: Armies were not yet gathered; Zhen men broke the long encirclement, set fire to Bao's camp; Bao could not resist and retreated to hold Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou broke out, burned Bao's camp; he fled to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 鎮人悉毀晉之營壘，取其芻粟，數日不盡。

translations.literal: Zhen men destroyed all Jin camps and took their fodder and grain; for days it was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Jin stores for days.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞之，以昭義節度使兼中書令李嗣昭為北面招討使，以代寶。

translations.literal: The prince heard it and made Zhaoyi military commissioner and chief councilor Li Sizhao northern campaign commissioner to replace Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The prince replaced Bao with Li Sizhao as northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，蜀軍使王承綱女將嫁，蜀主取之入宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Shu army commissioner Wang Chenggang's daughter was to marry; the Shu ruler took her into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: the Shu ruler seized Wang Chenggang's daughter on her wedding day.

sentences.zh: 承綱請之，蜀主怒，流於茂州。

translations.literal: Chenggang begged for her; the Shu ruler was angry and exiled him to Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggang pleaded; the ruler exiled him to Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 女聞父得罪，自殺。

translations.literal: The daughter, hearing her father was punished, killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: She killed herself on hearing of his punishment.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，張處瑾遣兵千人迎糧於九門，李嗣昭設伏於故營，邀擊之，殺獲殆盡，餘五人匿於牆墟間，嗣昭環馬而射之，鎮兵發矢中其腦，嗣昭箙中矢盡，拔矢於腦以射之，一發而殪。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Zhang Chujin sent a thousand men to meet grain at Jiumen; Li Sizhao ambushed at the old camp and attacked; nearly all were killed or captured; five men hid in ruined walls; Sizhao circled his horse shooting; Zhen soldiers shot an arrow into his brain; Sizhao's quiver was empty, pulled the arrow from his brain to shoot, and one shot killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Sizhao ambushed grain escorts at Jiumen, took an arrow in the brain, pulled it out, and killed his shooter before dying.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，還營，創流血不止。

translations.literal: Night fell and he returned to camp; the wound bled without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He bled without cease that night.

sentences.zh: 是夕卒。

translations.literal: That night he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that night.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞之，不御酒肉者累日。

translations.literal: The prince heard it and abstained from meat and wine for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The prince mourned without meat or wine for days.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭遺命：悉以澤、潞兵授節度判官任圜，使督諸軍攻鎮州，號令如一，鎮人不知嗣昭之死。

translations.literal: Sizhao's last order: give all Ze and Lu troops to circuit judge Ren Yuan to direct attack on Zhenzhou with unified command; Zhen men did not know Sizhao had died.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao left Ze and Lu troops to Ren Yuan; Zhenzhou did not know he was dead.

sentences.zh: 圜，三原人也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a man of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉王以天雄馬步都指揮使、振武節度使李存進為北面招討使。

translations.literal: The prince made Tianxiong horse and foot commander and Zhenwu military commissioner Li Cunjin northern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunjin became northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 命嗣昭諸子護喪歸葬晉陽；

translations.literal: He ordered Sizhao's sons to escort the coffin to bury at Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao's sons were to bury him at Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 其子繼能不受命，帥父牙兵數千，自行營擁喪歸潞州。

translations.literal: his son Jineng did not accept the order and led several thousand of his father's guard troops from the field camp, themselves escorting the coffin to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: son Jineng defied orders and led guard troops to Luzhou with the coffin.

sentences.zh: 晉王遣母弟存渥馳騎追諭之，兄弟俱忿，欲殺存渥，存渥逃歸。

translations.literal: The prince sent his mother's younger brother Cunwo on fast horse to overtake and instruct them; the brothers were all angry and wished to kill Cunwo; Cunwo fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Cunwo fled when the brothers meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭七子、繼儔、繼韜、繼達、繼忠、繼能、繼襲、繼遠。

translations.literal: Sizhao's seven sons: Jichou, Jitao, Jida, Jizhong, Jineng, Jixi, Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao's seven sons: Jichou, Jitao, Jida, Jizhong, Jineng, Jixi, Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 繼儔為澤州刺史，當襲爵，素懦弱。

translations.literal: Jichou was Zezhou prefect and should inherit the title; he was always timid.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Jichou of Ze was timid.

sentences.zh: 繼韜凶狡，囚繼儔於別室，詐令士卒劫己為留後，繼韜陽讓，以事白晉王。

translations.literal: Jitao was fierce and treacherous; he imprisoned Jichou in another room and had soldiers falsely seize him as regent; Jitao pretended to yield and reported to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao imprisoned Jichou and seized power, then feigned yielding.

sentences.zh: 晉王以用兵方殷，不得已，改昭義軍曰安義，以繼韜為留後。

translations.literal: The prince, with war pressing, had no choice; he changed Zhaoyi Army to Anyi and made Jitao regent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince renamed Zhaoyi to Anyi and made Jitao regent.

sentences.zh: 閻寶慚憤，疽發於背，甲戌卒。

translations.literal: Yan Bao was ashamed and indignant; an abscess broke out on his back; on jiaxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao's back abscess killed him on jiaxu.

sentences.zh: 漢主巖用術者言，游梅口鎮避災。

translations.literal: Han ruler Yan, using a diviner's words, toured Meikou town to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Yan toured Meikou to avoid disaster per diviners.

sentences.zh: 其地近閩之西鄙，閩將王延美將兵襲之，未至數十里，偵者告之，巖遁逃僅免。

translations.literal: The place was near Min's western border; Min general Wang Yanmei led troops to raid; scouts reported when still several tens of li away; Yan fled and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Min's Wang Yanmei nearly caught Yan at Meikou; he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉，晉李存進至鎮州，營於東垣渡，夾滹沱水為壘。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on yiyou Li Cunjin reached Zhenzhou and encamped at Dongyuan Ford, building ramparts on both sides of the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, yiyou: Li Cunjin camped at Dongyuan Ford on the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 晉衛州刺史李存儒，本姓楊，名婆兒，以俳優得幸於晉王。

translations.literal: Jin Weizhou prefect Li Cunru, original surname Yang, childhood name Po'er, won favor as an actor with the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunru of Weizhou, once the actor Yang Po'er, was the prince's favorite.

sentences.zh: 頗有膂力，晉王賜姓名，以為刺史；

translations.literal: He had considerable strength; the prince gave him a name and made him prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Strong and favored, he was made prefect;

sentences.zh: 志事掊斂，防城卒皆征月課縱歸。

translations.literal: his aim was extortion; garrison soldiers were all levied monthly and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: he extorted the garrison with monthly levies.

sentences.zh: 八月，莊宅使段凝與步軍都指揮使張朗引兵夜渡河襲之，詰旦登城，執存儒，遂克衛州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, estate commissioner Duan Ning and infantry commander Zhang Lang led troops by night across the river to raid; at dawn they mounted the wall, seized Cunru, and took Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Duan Ning and Zhang Lang took Weizhou at dawn and captured Cunru.

sentences.zh: 戴思遠又與凝攻陷淇門、共城、新鄉，於是澶州之西，相州之南，皆為梁有；

translations.literal: Dai Siyuan again with Ning took Qimen, Gongcheng, and Xinxiang; thus west of Duanzhou and south of Xiangzhou all belonged to Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan and Ning took Qimen, Gongcheng, Xinxiang—west of Duan and south of Xiang fell to Liang;

sentences.zh: 晉人失軍儲三之一，梁軍復振。

translations.literal: Jin lost a third of army stores; Liang armies revived.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lost a third of stores; Liang revived.

sentences.zh: 帝以張朗為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Zhang Lang Weizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang Emperor made Zhang Lang Weizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 朗，徐州人也。

translations.literal: Lang was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lang came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊寅朔，張處瑾使其弟處球乘李存進無備，將兵七千人奄至東垣渡。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on wuyin the new moon, Zhang Chujin sent his brother Chuqiu with seven thousand men to surprise Dongyuan Ford while Jin cavalry also went to Zhenzhou walls—the two did not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuyin: Chuqiu surprised Dongyuan Ford with seven thousand while Jin horse also neared Zhenzhou walls—they missed each other.

sentences.zh: 時晉之騎兵亦向鎮州城下，兩不相遇。

translations.literal: Zhen troops reached Cunjin's camp gate; Cunjin in disarray led a dozen men fighting on the bridge; Zhen retreated; Jin cavalry cut their rear and struck from both sides; Zhen troops were nearly all destroyed; Cunjin also died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen troops hit Cunjin's camp; he fought on the bridge with a dozen men; Jin cavalry struck from behind; Cunjin died and Zhen troops were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵及存進營門，存進狼狽引十餘人斗於橋上，鎮兵退，晉騎兵斷其後，夾擊之，鎮兵殆盡，存進亦戰沒。

translations.literal: The prince made Han and tribal horse and foot commander Li Cunshen northern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The prince named Li Cunshen northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉王以蕃漢馬步總管李存審為北面招討使。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou's strength and food were exhausted; Chujin sent envoys to headquarters to request surrender; before reply Cunshen's army reached the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Chujin begged to surrender before Cunshen's army reached the walls.

sentences.zh: 鎮州食竭力盡，處瑾遣使詣行台請降，未報，存審兵至城下。

translations.literal: At midnight on bingzi Li Zaifeng was inner agent, secretly lowering ropes to admit Jin troops; by dawn they had all mounted; they seized Chujin, brothers, family, and faction Gao Meng, Li Xu, Qi Jian and sent them to headquarters; Zhao people all begged to eat them; Zhang Wenli's corpse was dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Li Zaifeng let Jin troops in; Chujin was seized; Zhao people devoured the captives; Wenli's corpse was torn apart in the market.

sentences.zh: 丙午夜，城中將李再豐為內應，密投縋以納晉兵，比明畢登，執處瑾兄弟家人及其黨高濛、李翥、齊儉送行台，趙人皆請而食之，磔張文禮屍於市。

translations.literal: An old Zhao attendant found the prince's remains in the ashes; the prince ordered sacrifice and burial.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant found Prince Yin's bones in the ashes; the prince buried them with rites.

sentences.zh: 趙王故侍者得趙王遺骸於灰燼中，晉王命祭而葬之。

translations.literal: Zhao general Fu Xi was made Chengde military commissioner; Wu Zhen was made Zhaozhou prefect; Zhao Renzhen Shenzhou; Li Zaifeng Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi became Chengde commissioner; Wu Zhen Zhaozhou; Zhao Renzhen Shenzhou; Li Zaifeng Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 以趙將符習為成德節度使，烏震為趙州刺史，趙仁貞為深州刺史，李再豐為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen was a man of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen came from Xindu.

sentences.zh: 震，信都人也。

translations.literal: Xi dared not accept Chengde and said: "The late lord has no heir and is not yet buried—I should wear mourning to bury him and then await orders."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi refused Chengde until he had buried Prince Yin in mourning.

sentences.zh: 符習不敢當成德，辭曰：「故使無後而未葬，習當斬衰以葬之，俟禮畢聽命。」

translations.literal: After burial he went to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he reported to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 既葬，即詣行台。

translations.literal: Zhao people asked the prince to also hold Chengde military commissioner; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao asked the prince to hold Chengde; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 趙人請晉王兼領成德節度使，從之。

translations.literal: The prince cut Xiang and Wei to establish Yining Army and made Xi its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He created Yining from Xiang and Wei and made Xi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉王割相、衛二州置義寧軍，以習為節度使。

translations.literal: Xi declined: "Weibo is a hegemon's seat and cannot be divided—I wish for one Henan commission and will take it myself."
translations.idiomatic: Xi declined: give me a Henan commission instead.

sentences.zh: 習辭曰：「魏博霸府，不可分也，願得河南一鎮，習自取之。」

translations.literal: He was therefore made Tianping military commissioner and southeast campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Tianping and southeast campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃以為天平節度使、東南面招討使。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen was added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 加李存審兼侍中。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on wuyin, Jin Special Advance and Hezhong overseer Zhang Chengye died; Lady Cao went to his house and wore mourning like a child or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, wuyin: Zhang Chengye died; Lady Cao mourned as kin.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅，晉特進、河東監軍使張承業卒，曹太夫人詣其第，為之行服，如子侄之禮。

translations.literal: The prince heard of his death and abstained from food for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The prince fasted many days.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞其喪，不食者累日。

translations.literal: The prince heard of his death and abstained from food for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The prince heard and fasted for many days.

sentences.zh: 命河東留守判官何瓚代知河東軍府事。

translations.literal: He ordered Hezhong regent judge He Zan to act as Hezhong military government.
translations.idiomatic: He Zan was ordered to administer Hezhong military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉王以魏博觀察判官晉陽張憲兼鎮冀觀察判官，權鎮州軍府事。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the prince made Weibo observation judge Jinyang Zhang Xian also Zhenji observation judge, acting Zhenzhou military government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the prince named Zhang Xian of Jinyang to also judge Zhenji and act for Zhenzhou military government.

sentences.zh: 魏州稅多逋負，晉王以讓司錄濟陰趙季良，季良曰：「殿下何時當平河南？」

translations.literal: Weizhou taxes were much in arrears; the prince blamed recorder Jiyin Zhao Jiliang; Jiliang said: "When will Your Highness pacify Henan?"
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou taxes were in arrears; the prince rebuked Zhao Jiliang, who asked, "When will Your Highness pacify Henan?"

sentences.zh: 王怒曰：「汝職在督稅，職之不修，何敢預我軍事！」

translations.literal: 」The prince angrily said: "Your duty is to supervise taxes; if you do not perform your office, how dare you meddle in my military affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince snapped, "Your job is tax collection—how dare you lecture me on war!"

sentences.zh: 季良對曰：「殿下方謀攻取而不愛百姓，一旦百姓離心，恐河北亦非殿下之有，況河南乎！」

translations.literal: 」Jiliang replied: "Your Highness plots conquest yet does not cherish the people—once the people turn away, I fear Hebei too may not remain yours, let alone Henan!"
translations.idiomatic: 」Jiliang answered, "You seek conquest but not the people's hearts—lose them and you lose Hebei before Henan!"

sentences.zh: 王悅，謝之。

translations.literal: 」The prince was pleased and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince relented and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 自是重之，每預謀議。

translations.literal: From then he was esteemed and joined every deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was valued in every council.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹改元天贊。

translations.literal: That year Khitan changed the era name to Tianzan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Khitan adopted the era name Tianzan.

sentences.zh: 大封王躬乂，性殘忍，海軍統帥王建殺之，自立，復稱高麗王，以開州為東京，平壤為西京。

translations.literal: Great Feng ruler Gong Yi was cruel; navy commander Wang Jian killed him, restored himself, again styled King of Goryeo, made Kaesong the eastern capital and Pyongyang the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yi of Great Feng was cruel. Wang Jian of the navy killed him, took the throne, restored the title King of Goryeo, and made Kaesong the eastern capital and Pyongyang the western.

sentences.zh: 建儉約寬厚，國人安之。

translations.literal: Jian was frugal and generous; the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was frugal and magnanimous, and the realm was calm.
